This counts itself, other played Treasures, played Actions, and any Duration cards (such as {card:Caravan} from Dominion: Seaside) played on your previous turn.

It only counts cards currently in play, not ones that were in play but left; for example if you played a {card:Pillage} (from Dominion: Dark Ages) this turn, you will have trashed it, so it will not count for Horn of Plenty.
This is a non-Supply pile; you can only gain a Horse from it when a card tells you to gain a Horse, not with cards like {card:Falconer} or {card:Displace}.
If you use a card like {card:Mastermind} to play a Horse multiple times, you get +2 Cards and +1 Action for each play, even though you can only return the Horse once.

For example, if another player plays {card:Followers}, you could reveal and set aside two Horse Traders from your hand, then gain a {card:Curse} but discard no cards, as you would only have three cards in hand at that point.
If the game ends while Horse Traders is set aside, it is returned to its owner's deck before scoring; this can matter for alt-VP cards such as {card:Gardens}.
When you gain this, you may discard any number of Treasure cards from your hand, to gain that many {card:Horse|Horses} from their pile.
If a Hovel is revealed when playing {card:Ambassador}, it is not returned to the Supply (since it is not in the Supply) and opponents do not gain a copy of it.

Cards with multiple types can be chosen for any matching type. For example, if the revealed cards were {card:Stronghold}, {card:Copper}, {card:Silver}, you would have to take Stronghold as the Action, would choose between Silver and Copper as the Treasure, and would get no Victory card. Then you would discard the unchosen Treasure.
Idol cares how many Idols you have in play, not how many you have played this turn; some cards can make those numbers different (e.g. {card:Counterfeit} from Dark Ages).
Receiving either {card:The Sea's Gift} or {card:The Wind's Gift} may draw you Actions that you normally can't play in your Buy phase.
Ill-Gotten Gains is not an Attack, and gaining it is not playing an Attack; cards like {card:Moat} do not work against it.

It does not matter if you played the Action card this turn, only that it is not in play when you play Imp; you can use Imp to play a card that you played but trashed and so do not have in play, like a {card:Pixie} you trashed, but cannot use it to play a card you did not play this turn that is still in play, such as a {card:Secret Cave} from your previous turn.

If you put cards into your hand using Improve (e.g. you trash a {card:Fortress}, or gain a {card:Den of Sin}), they will get discarded during the remainder of Clean-up (unless you use {card:Coastal Haven}).
If you use Improve to gain a 2nd copy of Improve, and then play it with {card:Innovation}, you can trash another Action from play.
Because Improve triggers during Clean-up, if you use it to gain or trash a {card:Trail}, you can't use the Trail's Reaction.

You can trash a Duration card from play if it has no abilities set up for future turns. If, after you trash a Duration card, something happens that would cause it to *try* to set up abilities for future turns, the future abilities don't happen because the Duration has already left play. For instance, you can trash a {card:Taskmaster} from play if you haven't gained a {cost:5}-cost card yet. Even if you gain a card costing {cost:5} later in the Clean-up phase, Taskmaster's abilities will not be activated because it has already left play.

If you trash a {card:Cargo Ship} from play that hasn't set aside a card yet, then when you gain a card after trashing it, Cargo Ship *can* still set the gained card aside—but the set-aside card will be stranded and never be put in your hand.

If {card:Garrison} has no tokens on it at the start of Clean-up, you can trash it with Improve. But if you then gain a card before resolving Improve (say, via a different copy of Improve), that puts a token on Garrison and it's no longer eligible to be trashed.
This doesn't happen when you gain Infirmary without paying for it (such as with {card:Horn of Plenty}).

In games using a Way, you can apply the Way when overpaying for Infirmary. For instance, you could buy Infirmary for {cost:7} and play the Infirmary four times using {card:Way of the Sheep} to get a total of {coin:+8}, meaning you'd end up with more {cost:} than you had before buying the Infirmary (which you could then spend if you have an additional +Buy).
This is not gaining a card, and does not count for things that care about gaining, such as {card:Treasure Hunter}; however at the end of the game, include the card in your deck when scoring.
Normally that means you will discard it that turn, but if the card is something like {card:Throne Room} and used to play a Duration card, it will stay out the same way Throne Room itself would have.
All Estates are affected, including ones in the Supply and ones other players have; for example this means you could gain one with {card:Seaway}.
The card cannot be a Command card; Command cards are certain cards that can play other cards without moving them, including {card:Band of Misfits}, {card:Overlord}, and {card:Captain}.
Inheritance affects Estates in the trash and in other players' decks and hands. This means that they can be gained with {card:Lurker}, discarded by {card:Rabble}, and so on.
It is no one's turn when scoring, this means that Estates will not count for Landmarks/Victory cards that care about Actions (like {card:Orchard} or {card:Vineyard}).

For example, gaining an Estate doesn't activate any on-gain effects of the Action card you've Inherited; Inheriting a {card:Crown} or {card:Werewolf} does not allow you to play Estates in the Buy or Night phases; Inheriting a Reaction card does not allow you to react with Estates the way you would react with the Reaction card; etc.

Under rare circumstances (involving a combination of certain Reaction cards, {card:Way of the Mouse}, and {card:Vassal}) it can be possible to play an Estate (if it's an Action card) on *another* player's turn. Whether or not an Estate is an Action card on another player's turn depends on whether *they* have bought Inheritance, not whether you have. If you do play an Estate on another player's turn, it plays the card with your Estate token on it as usual, not the card with their Estate token.
Since Inheritance adds two types to Estates, this affects how Estates will interact with cards like {card:Courtier} and {card:Falconer}.

If the Inherited pile is a split pile (from Empires or Allies), players take cards from the pile in turn order. So in a 6-player game with the {card:Townsfolk} pile, the first four players get a {card:Town Crier}, and the next two get a {card:Blacksmith}.

Anything that cares about shuffling (e.g. {card:Star Chart} or {card:Order of Masons}) can be used when you shuffle your entire deck. You may look through all the cards in your deck when using their abilities.
If you gain an Inn and you don't shuffle it into your deck, it can still get moved by other abilities (like {card:Changeling} and {card:Gatekeeper}).

If you gain an Inn onto your deck (with e.g. {card:Artificer}), shuffling your deck will cause other abilities (like Changeling and Gatekeeper) to lose track. This is true even if Inn is the only card in your deck, or if you keep Inn on top of your deck (with either Star Chart or {card:Order of Astrologers}).
If gaining an Action card causes you to gain an Inn (e.g. it was {card:Border Village}, or you played a {card:Charm}), you can shuffle both that Action card and the Inn back in your deck.

Innovation can't play a card unless it can physically put it into play. For example, if you gain a card to your discard pile and use {card:Sleigh} to move the card to the top of your deck, the stop-moving rule prevents Innovation from moving the card again from your deck into play, and so it can't be played.
If you gain a {card:Duplicate} and then play it with Innovation, you can call it immediately to gain another Duplicate.
Duration cards that you played on previous turns that are still in play, are in play; cards that have left play somehow, like a {card:Mining Village} (from Intrigue) trashing itself, are not in play.

When you gain a Loot and play it, the No Visiting rule is **not** in effect; you gain the Loot to your discard pile, and then any on-gain triggers are activated, and then you play the Loot. If an on-gain trigger moves the Loot out of your discard pile (for example, you reveal a {card:Watchtower} to top-deck the Loot, the stop-moving rule prevents you from playing it.

If you gain an Inventor with Inventor and then play the gained Inventor with {card:Innovation}, the first Inventor's cost reduction hasn't kicked in yet, so the second Inventor can still only gain a card costing {cost:4}.
Even if you trash an Inventor from the play area (e.g., with {card:Procession}), the cost reduction remains in force till the end of the turn.
If you have 2 copies of a card in Exile, and only one of them was Exiled with Invest, you can use {card:Transport} to topdeck the non-Invested copy.
If you play the same Investment twice (e.g. with {card:Crown}) and trash it on the first play for {vp:}, then you can't trash it on the second play for {vp:}.
A card with 2 types gives you both bonuses; if you use Ironworks to gain a {card:Mill}, you both draw a card and get +1 Action.
If you gain a card that has none of the listed types (such as {card:Curse} or {card:Ghost Town}), you get no bonus.
If you gain an {card:Estate} after buying {card:Inheritance}, you get +1 Action and +1 Card.
For example, if you gain a Mill and play it with {card:Innovation}, you'll get +1 Action and +1 Card after you finish playing the Mill.
During a {card:Possession} turn, Ironworks will never give you any bonus (see the blue dog rule).

If the gained card is trashed or returned to its pile after being gained, for example by revealing {card:Watchtower} to trash it, Ironworks still gives bonuses for the card even though it is no longer owned by the player when the bonuses are resolved.
If you {card:Throne Room} an Island, you set aside two cards with it.

If you {card:Procession} an Island, you set it aside with a card, then you set aside another card; you do not trash the Island because it has already been set aside, but you do gain a card costing {cost:1} more than the Island.
If you play {card:Voyage} the same turn you spend Favors with Island Folk, you've hit the "but not a 3rd turn" limit, so you will have to choose which extra turn to take.
If you are {card:Possession|Possessed}, and they make you spend Favors for Island Folk, you take an Island Folk turn, and then take your normal turn.

Although it is visible to all players which card is being discarded, it is not considered to be "revealed" by the game rules even though the original official FAQ below used the word "revealed". This means that a {card:Patron} discarded by Jester will not produce Coffers.

If a Jester makes you discard a Reaction card like {card:Tunnel} or {card:Village Green} that says "When you discard this... you may reveal it," you can choose whether or not to "reveal" it for its effect.
If a card plays this multiple times (e.g. {card:King's Cache}), then when you put this on the bottom of your deck, that card will remain in play until the Clean-up phase.
If you set up multiple extra turns at once (e.g. one from Journey, one from {card:Voyage}), you choose one turn to take, and the others fail.
If you are {card:Possession|Possessed}, and they make you buy Journey, anything they made you play will stay in play, you take a Journey turn, and then take your normal turn.

Cards with "while this is in play" abilities can continue to function, and the cards are in play for things that care about that, such as {card:Swamp Shacks}; otherwise, the cards being in play just means you won't draw them that turn.
Cards that would have stayed in play anyway (e.g. a {card:Longship} played on the turn you bought Journey) stay in play for that reason, and do whatever they normally do.

Almost all "while this is in play" abilities have either received errata (e.g. {card:Quarry}) or been removed (e.g. {card:Talisman}). The exception is {card:Urchin}, which you can play during your regular turn, and then trash into a {card:Mercenary} on the Journey turn.

If you play {card:Lich} and buy Journey on the same turn, your cards remain in play, the Journey turn gets skipped, and you'll discard those cards from play during the next Clean-up (yours or another player's).

If you buy Journey, then any effects that care about cards that you discard from play this turn (e.g. {card:Improve} and {card:Scheme}) will do nothing. However, some effects trigger at the start of Clean-up (e.g. {card:Alchemist} and {card:Walled Village}), and they trigger normally.
Journey's restriction only applies to your cards. Any cards that other players play (e.g. {card:Mapmaker}) will be discarded normally.
Actions that have become Treasures via {card:Capitalism} do not count at the end of the game, as it is no longer your turn.
However, {card:Curse|Curses} do count as Treasures at the end of the game in games with {card:Charlatan}.
If the card is an Attack and other players want to use cards like {card:Moat}, you gain the card before they choose to use Moat or not.
If you play a {card:Stockpile} after a Kiln, you gain a Stockpile first, may discard Stockpiles from Exile, and then you Exile your played Stockpile.
If you {card:Throne Room} a Kiln and gain a Kiln, you can react with {card:Sheepdog}, but since you haven't resolved Kiln a second time yet, you won't gain a copy of Sheepdog.
If you play Kiln, play {card:Conspirator}, gain a 2nd Conspirator and play it with {card:Innovation}, both Conspirators will give +1 Card and +1 Action.
If you remove the last {sun} at the start of your turn (e.g. you play a {card:Poet} with {card:Delay}), you'll gain 2 Actions to your hand.
If you King's Cache a {card:Capital}, you end up with 6 debt when the Capital is discarded, not 18.
This is similar to {card:Throne Room}, but plays the Action three times rather than twice.

For example if you start a turn by playing King's Court on {card:Village}, you would draw a card, get +2 Actions, draw another card, get +2 Actions again, draw a 3rd card, and get +2 Actions again, leaving you with 6 Actions.
If trashing a card causes you to gain a Gold (e.g. you discard a {card:Market Square}), that will let you gain a card costing up to {cost:2} more.
The pile does not get a token for {card:Trade Route} (from Prosperity), even if the top Knight is a Victory card.

{card:Dame Josephine} is also a Victory card, worth {vp:2} at the end of the game. The Knight pile is not a Victory pile though, and does not get a counter for {card:Trade Route} (from Prosperity) even if Dame Josephine starts on top.
If you choose to use the Knights with {card:Black Market} (a promotional card), put a Knight directly into the Black Market deck, rather than using the randomizer card.
{card:Sir Martin} only costs {cost:4}, though the other Knights all cost {cost:5}. When Sir Martin is the top card of the pile, it can be gained with an {card:Armory} and so on.
During a turn with {card:Possession}, no players will get any {vp:} from this.
Resolve the Treasure before putting Landing Party on your deck; for example if the Treasure is {card:Figurine}, you'd draw 2 cards before putting Landing Party on top.
It's okay if the Treasure has more types, including Action (like {card:Spell Scroll}).

Duration cards that you played on previous turns that have an effect at the beginning of this turn, such as {card:Caravan}, don't have any effect on whether you can top-deck Landing Party. Neither do Reserve cards put into play at the beginning of the turn by calling them, such as {card:Transmogrify}. Only the first card you actually play on the turn, and whether or not it is a Treasure, matters for Landing Party.

The first card you play on your turn can be one that you play from your hand in the normal way, or it can be one played as a result of an "at the start of your turn" instruction, such as that of {card:Piazza}, {card:Reap}, or {card:Royal Galley}. What matters for start-of-your-turn instructions is whether they are actually telling you to "play" something.

If the first Treasure you play is a {card:Spell Scroll}, which gains and plays a Landing Party, that will make you topdeck your other Landing Parties, but not the one you just played (it triggers off the *next* time your first card played is a Treasure).

If you play a Treasure on someone *else's* turn (for example, if you gain a {card:Buried Treasure} as a result of a {card:Barbarian} attack and immediately play it), that can top-deck your Landing Parties.
Unlike {card:Cavalry}, Launch draws you a card after ending your Buy phase. So if ending your Buy phase makes you put a {card:Treasury} onto your deck, you will draw it with Launch.
If you gain extra Favors at the start of your Buy phase (e.g. you discard a {card:Weaver} to {card:Arena}, and then gain a {card:Sycophant}), that may give you more {coin:+} from this.
If you take multiple Buy phases in a turn (with e.g. {card:Villa} or {card:Cavalry}), you can get {coin:+} from this multiple times.
If you have 3 Favors, and you use {card:Throne Room} on {card:Underling}, you only get {coin:+1} from League of Shopkeepers.
However, if you have 3 Favors, play an Underling, and then replay it with either {card:Royal Carriage} or {card:Citadel}, League of Shopkeepers will trigger twice, and you can get {coin:+2} from it.
If you have 10+ Favors and play either a {card:Bauble} or a {card:Contract}, you can get +1 Action in your Buy phase; this won't let you play more Actions from your hand.
If you gain a {card:Sycophant}, get +2 Favors, and then play it with {card:Innovation}, the 2 Favors will count for League of Shopkeepers.

However, if you gain a {card:Guildmaster} and play it with {card:Innovation}, the Guildmaster will give you +1 Favor from gaining itself. However, you won't get that Favor in time for League of Shopkeepers.
Players wishing to respond to the Attack (e.g. with {card:Moat}) must do so before you choose whether or not to reveal a {card:Gold}.
Cards that were in play but no longer are - e.g. a {card:Pixie} you trashed - do not count.

This checks for the number of cards you have in play after gaining the {card:Gold}. This means that if you have 6 cards in play (including the Leprechaun), you can react to the gained Gold with a {card:Sheepdog}, and that will count for the {card:Wish}.
If you set aside any Action-Reaction cards that care about being discarded (such as {card:Village Green} or {card:Trail}), you resolve their Reactions after you finish drawing.
You can skip an extra turn, like one from {card:Voyage}.

When you skip an extra turn (e.g. {card:Voyage}), you're also skipping its Clean-up phase. This means you'll discard the Voyage from play during the Clean-up of the next turn that happens (either yours or another player's).
It also means if you play Lich and {card:Outpost} in the same turn, you draw 3 cards during Clean-up, skip the Outpost turn, and then you keep that 3-card hand for your next turn.

If you'll take multiple extra turns at the same time (e.g. one from Voyage and one from {card:Island Folk}), you can choose what order they happen in. The first turn you take will be the one that gets skipped by Lich.
However, Lich cannot skip a turn that never happens. So if on an Island Folk turn, you play Lich and Voyage, Lich will not skip that {card:Voyage} turn, because Voyage won't let you 3 turns in a row.

Cards that check what you did on a previous turn (like {card:Smugglers}) will check the turn that you actually played. So if you skip a turn with Lich, and the next player plays a Smugglers, it doesn't check the skipped turn, and instead checks the last turn you played (which will usually be the same turn that you played Lich).

If on the same turn, you play Lich and a Duration that says "until your next turn..." (e.g. {card:Monkey} or {card:Highwayman}), that Duration's effect will last until the next turn you take (i.e. it extends past your skipped turn).
A trashed Lich gains a card cheaper than it, and not a card that costs up to {cost:5}. This may matter if cards have changed cost (e.g. due to {card:Family of Inventors}).

If you trash multiple cards at once, you put them all into the trash, then resolve on-trash effects. So if you use {card:Sentinel} to trash a Lich and a {card:Sycophant}, the Lich can gain the Sycophant.

If you {card:Possession|Possess} a player and make them trash a Lich, you can choose to either put the Lich in their discard pile, or set it aside, to put in their discard pile at the end of the turn. Either way, you will still gain a cheaper card from the trash.

When you trash this from the Supply (with {card:Lurker}), you still discard the Lich (into your own discard pile) and gain a cheaper card from the trash. Discarding the Lich this way doesn't count as gaining it.

Lighthouse only protects you from Attacks if the Lighthouse is in effect *when the Attack is played*, regardless of when the Attack's effects would hit you. So for example, if you get attacked by {card:Corsair} or {card:Blockade}, playing a Lighthouse afterwards will not protect you from their delayed attacks.
This protects you for the rest of the turn when you play it. So for example, if after playing a Lighthouse, you gain a {card:Duchy}, this will protect you from another player's {card:Black Cat}.
This includes getting attacked at the start of your next turn; if you trash a {card:Hunting Grounds} with {card:Donate} and gain a Duchy, Lighthouse won't protect you from Black Cat.
This is cumulative; for example, if you use {card:Mastermind} to play a Livery three times, then each card you gain that turn costing {cost:4} or more will come with three {card:Horse|Horses}.

This checks the cost of the card as it's being gained, not after. So if you gain a {card:Fisherman} with an empty discard pile, you will not gain a {card:Horse}, because Fisherman cost {cost:2} when you gained it.
If you gain a Livery and play it with {card:Innovation}, you will gain a Horse.

If you gain a copy of Livery with either {card:Disciple} or {card:Specialist}, you will gain a Horse. But if you gain a copy of Livery with {card:Kiln}, you won't gain a Horse, because you haven't followed Livery's instructions yet.

If you trash a card costing a {potion} or {debt:}, the cheaper cards are those that cost less {cost:}, {potion}, or {debt:} and also don't cost more {cost:}, {potion}, or {debt:}. For example, {card:Village} and {card:University} are both cheaper than {card:Alchemist}. {card:Ruined Village} and {card:Engineer} are both cheaper than {card:City Quarter}. Nothing is cheaper than {cost:0}.

The three cards you look at are not considered to still be the top cards of your deck *while* you are resolving Lookout. Thus, for example, if you trash a card with an on-trash draw bonus, such as {card:Overgrown Estate}, you will not draw one of the remaining two cards you're looking at, but rather the next one down.

If a card is put on top of your deck while you are resolving Lookout (for instance, by discarding a {card:Tunnel}, gaining a {card:Gold}, and top-decking it due to {card:Progress}) then when you return the third card to your deck it will go on top of the card you just put there.
Lost in the Woods stays in front of you turn after turn, until another player takes it with a {card:Fool}.
For example Lurker can trash {card:Nobles} from the Supply and can gain Nobles from the trash.

Trashing a card from the Supply will activate its when-trash abilities. For example, if you trash a {card:Fortress} from the Supply, it will move itself into your hand; if you trash {card:Hunting Grounds} from the Supply, you gain a {card:Duchy} or 3 {card:Estate|Estates}.
Trashing from the Supply does *not* allow you to react with {card:Market Square}, because it isn't one of your cards.
You can only trash the top card of a Supply pile, which may matter with split piles or {card:Knights}.
This card is not in the Supply; it can only be obtained via {card:Hermit}.
Normally nothing will prevent you from returning Madman to the Madman pile, but you may fail to due to playing Madman twice via cards like {card:Throne Room}.

So, for example, if you {card:Procession} a Madman, you will get +2 Actions, return Madman to the Madman pile, draw a card per card in your hand, get another +2 Actions, fail to return Madman and so not draw cards the second time, fail to trash Madman, and then gain an Action card costing exactly {cost:1} if you can.

Since you can play Treasures in whatever order you want, having (for example) multiple {card:Copper|Coppers} you want to play needn't prevent you from trashing your Magic Lamp for {card:Wish|Wishes}. Simply play one Copper to count as one of your six unique cards in play, play your Magic Lamp, and then play the rest of your Coppers.
If you reveal a [{card:Farm}] (from Intrigue), you both put it into your hand and gain a Magpie, since it is both a Treasure and a Victory card.
If the card you reveal belongs to none of those types, such as {card:Curse}, {card:Hovel}, or {card:Vampire}, nothing happens.
If you gain Marchland to your hand (such as via {card:Artisan}), it can be one of the cards you discard for +{cost:}.
If the card they draw is a Reaction that triggers on an attack (such as {card:Moat} or {card:Caravan Guard}), they cannot use it (but they can keep it in their hand to use against a future attack).
Market Square has the same timing as "when you trash this" effects on other cards, such as {card:Cultist}, and you choose the order they happen in.
Market Square cannot be discarded if you trash a card you don't own, such as with {card:Lurker}.
If you trash a {card:Haunted Mirror}, you can discard Market Square for either a Gold or a {card:Ghost}, but not both.
If you gain Favors while resolving Market Towns (e.g. by playing a {card:Broker}), you may continue spending those Favors to keep playing Actions.
Market Towns does not specify that you re-enter your Action phase. Therefore, cards that give additional Action plays, such as {card:Village}, do not allow additional Actions to be played.

If you gain a {card:Villa} or {card:Cavalry} in the middle of resolving Market Towns, you'll end your Buy phase (which will let you discard {card:Wine Merchant} and pay {cost:1} to {card:Pageant}), and then continue resolving other "at the start of Buy phase" abilities (such as {card:Arena} or Market Towns itself).
If you play {card:Leprechaun} and receive either {card:Envy} or {card:Delusion}, you return the corresponding State after you finish resolving Market Towns.
If you return {card:Deluded}, then use Market Towns to play Leprechaun and receive Envy, you'll be affected by Deluded and {card:Envious} at the same time.
For example if you trash a {card:Cage} with Maroon, you'll draw 4 cards, since it's a Treasure and a Duration, 2 types.
If the trashed card has a Trait, or is {card:Young Witch}'s Bane, that won't count as an extra type for Maroon.
{card:Inheritance}, {card:Capitalism}, {card:Charlatan}, and {card:Enlightenment} will add types to cards.
Players with no cards in hand (such as due to {card:Torturer}) are skipped over - they neither pass a card nor receive one.
This is not an Attack and so cannot be stopped with {card:Moat}.
Passed cards are not "gained" (which matters for some expansion cards, e.g. {card:Trader} from Dominion: Hinterlands).

Masquerade's mechanism for changing card ownership is unique in the game, since it uses the word "pass" to indicate a change of card ownership. The consequence of this wording is that the player receiving a passed card is not "gaining" it. So, for example, they cannot react to the card passing with {card:Watchtower}.

Playing these Actions does not use up Action plays. For example, if you Mastermind a {card:Bounty Hunter}, you will get +3 Actions total, and be able to play 4 Action cards after that - your normal one, plus 3 more for the +3 Actions.

If you Mastermind a {card:Horse}, you will get +2 Cards and +1 Action, return the Horse to its pile, get +2 Cards and +1 Action, fail to return the Horse since you already did, and get +2 Cards and +1 Action a third time and fail to return the Horse again.

Mastermind only stays in play for longer than normal if it plays a Duration card (such as a 2nd Mastermind). If it plays a {card:Throne Room} that plays a Duration, the Mastermind doesn't stay in play.

If Mastermind plays a Duration (such as a 2nd Mastermind), but you remove it from play (with e.g. {card:Way of the Horse}), the Mastermind doesn't stay in play (and the Duration's will not have any effect on your next turn).
This card is not in the Supply; it can only be obtained via {card:Urchin}.
Players responding to this Attack with cards like {card:Beggar} must choose to do so before you decide whether or not to trash two cards from your hand.
If you play the same Merchant multiple times (e.g. with {card:Throne Room}), each of the plays will give you {coin:+1} when you play the first Silver.

If you play Merchant after you play your first Silver (e.g. you played a Silver to buy a {card:Villa}, and then play a Merchant), you do not get {coin:+1} for the Silver you already played; you also do not get {coin:+1} if you play another Silver since it's not the first one you played.
However, if playing a Silver causes you to play a Merchant (e.g. you trash a {card:Catacombs} with {card:Sauna}, gain a Merchant, and play it with {card:Innovation}), you'll get {coin:+1}.
If you play this using a Way, or under the influence of {card:Enchantress}, you can still top-deck this when you discard it from play.
This counts all cards gained in your Buy phase, whether bought, or gained other ways, such as via {card:Ferryman}.
It does not count cards gained in your Action phase, such as with {card:Butcher}.
This is cumulative; if you play two Merchant Guilds, or play one twice via a card such as {card:Throne Room}, you will get +2 Coffers per card gained.
In rare cases (such as with {card:Villa}, from Empires), your Buy phase can end multiple times in a turn; Merchant Guild will happen each time it ends.
So you may acquire the Coffers from Merchant Guild, spend two of them to earn {cost:2}, and use the {cost:2} to discard {card:Wine Merchant|Wine Merchants} from your Tavern mat.

If you play Merchant Guild after your Buy phase (e.g. you gain it during the Night phase (with e.g. {card:Vampire}) or Clean-up (with e.g. {card:Improve}) and then play it with {card:Innovation}), you won't get any Coffers from it.
This is not discarding cards and does not trigger {card:Tunnel} (from Hinterlands).
This works if you gain this by buying it, or if you gain this in another way (such as {card:Ball} or {card:Anvil}).
If you take multiple Buy phases (with {card:Villa} or {card:Cavalry}), you can use Messenger's on-gain effect multiple times in the same turn.

If gaining a Treasure causes you to gain a Treasure (e.g. a {card:Fortune} that gains a {card:Gold}), and you've played multiple Mining Roads, you can play those Treasures in any order (i.e. you can play the Gold before playing the Fortune).
If you {card:Throne Room} a Mining Village, you cannot trash it twice (and so cannot get the {coin:+2} twice).
You only get {coin:+2} if Mining Village trashes itself, not if it is trashed in another way, for example by trashing it with {card:Steward}.
Players wishing to respond with e.g. {card:Moat} or {card:Diplomat} do so before you choose your option.
{card:Horse Traders} normally doesn't actually block an attack, but in the case of Minion it can.
If you gain this in your Action phase, such as with {card:Artisan}, you will usually not have any Treasures in play to trash.
If you gain a Mint with {card:Tiara} in play, you can put the Mint on your deck, regardless of whether you trash the Tiara before or afterwards.
If you have {card:Capitalism}, Mint can both gain and trash Action-Treasures.
If you played some {card:Copper|Coppers}, but trashed them all with Mint, that means you're allowed to buy a {card:Grand Market}.
If you first gain {card:Mandarin} and top-deck all your Treasures, gaining Mint won't trash any Treasures.
Mint can only gain copies from the Supply, so it can't gain copies of {card:Spoils}, Heirlooms, or Treasures from the {card:Black Market} deck.
If this hits you for a third time in a game, nothing will happen; you stay at {card:Twice Miserable}.
You can still buy Events, and play cards, and gain cards in ways other than buying them (such as gaining a {card:Silver} from {card:Amulet}), and exchange Travellers.
You cannot buy cards from {card:Black Market} during a Mission turn.
If you set up 2 extra turns at once (e.g. one from Mission, one from {card:Voyage}), you choose one turn to take, and the others fail.
If you are {card:Possession|Possessed}, and they make you buy Mission, you will take a Mission turn, and then take your normal turn.
An Attack card says "Attack" on the bottom line; in this set, {card:Bandit}, {card:Bureaucrat}, {card:Militia}, and {card:Witch} are Attacks.
The other player must play the Attack card; for example, you cannot reveal Moat when another player gains an {card:Ill-Gotten Gains}.
The played card must have the Attack type; for example, you cannot reveal Moat when another player plays a {card:Masquerade}.

Other players must reveal Moat before you resolve any abilities of the Attack you played. For example, you can see if anyone reveals a Moat before making your choice with {card:Minion}, and before deciding whether to play your Attack via a Way.

If you play this with {card:Elder} and pick both choices, you do them in the printed order, meaning you draw a card before gaining a card. This means you can't draw the card that you just gained. But if the card you draw is a Reaction that cares about gaining cards (such as {card:Sheepdog}), you can use it.
Normally, bought cards are then gained, but cards exchanged for (such as {card:Vampire} exchanging for {card:Bat}) are not gained.

Gaining cards while you trash to Monastery (for example, if you trash a {card:Hunting Grounds}) does not let you trash additional cards; you can only trash a number of cards equal to the number of cards gained that turn prior to playing Monastery.
This includes cards that the player gains on other players' turns, such as a {card:Curse} they gain on your turn via {card:Witch}.
If they gain an Attack card to make you discard to their {card:Skirmisher}, you'll first discard down to 3 cards, and then you'll draw a card from Monkey.

If they gain a {card:Berserker} and play it, you'll draw a card (from the cheaper card that their Berserker gains); then you'll discard down to 3 cards; then you'll draw another card (from the initial Berserker gain).
If your Monkey draws a Reaction that can react to the card they gained (e.g. they gained a Treasure and you draw a {card:Pirate}), you can immediately use it.
If the player to your right gains a {card:Province}, you can trash a {card:Fool's Gold} from your hand, and then draw the gained {card:Gold} with Monkey.

If you play this with {card:Way of the Chameleon}, you get {coin:+1} when the player to your right gains a card during your turn. Afterwards, you'll get +1 Card when that player gains a card, and +1 Card at the start of your next turn.

The Duration effect ends instantaneously when your next turn starts. So if another player gains a card at the start of your turn (e.g. you play a {card:Witch} with {card:Prepare}), Monkey won't draw you a card from that.
This only happens the first time a player gains a {card:Province}; it does not matter if the Province was bought or not, or if Provinces have left the pile earlier due to {card:Salt the Earth}.

If someone gains the first Province during a turn you are controlling with {card:Possession} (from Alchemy), "make all decisions" means you have control over how much {debt:} the Possessed player bids. If that player wins the bid, they take the {vp:8}, and you take the {debt:}. In practice (at least in a 2-player game), you force them to bid {debt:0}, and you can take {debt:1} for {vp:8}.
If you trash a {card:Fortress} or {card:Lich} with Mountain Shrine, it will leave the trash *before* Mountain Shrine checks if there are any Actions in the trash.
Names need to match exactly for you to get the card; for example {card:Sir Destry} and {card:Sir Martin} do not match.
The Action card stays in the trash; if an effect tries to move it, such as {card:Encampment} (from Empires) returning to the Supply, it will fail to move it.

Necromancer can be used on a card that trashes itself when played; if the card checks to see if it was trashed (such as {card:Pixie}), it was not, but if the card does not check (such as {card:Tragic Hero}), it will function normally.
Since the played card is not in play, "while this is in play" abilities (such as {card:Tracker|Tracker's}†) will not do anything.
Face-down cards in the trash can still be interacted with by cards other than Necromancer, such as {card:Lurker}, and you can still look at them if you want to know what they are.

The restriction on movement only applies to effects that would have moved the card out of the play area if it were played normally, for example, {card:Island} will fail to move itself out of the trash and onto your Island Mat, although any other effect will still apply, such as moving a card from your hand onto your Island Mat; if a card is looking to move a card out of the trash, it may move itself - thus, if you choose to play a Lurker, {card:Graverobber} or {card:Rogue} in the trash, it can gain itself out of the trash as a result.

Attempting to trash a card in the trash doesn't count as trashing. So if you try to trash a {card:Tragic Hero} in the trash, you won't gain any {vp:} from {card:Tomb}, and it won't activate {card:Sewers}.
Unlike {card:Band of Misfits}, Necromancer can play Command cards from the trash.
When a Necropolis is revealed when playing {card:Ambassador}, it is not returned to the Supply (since it is not in the Supply) and opponents do not gain a copy of it.

When Necropolis is played according to {card:Way of the Horse} or {card:Way of the Butterfly}, it has no pile to return to and remains in your play area. (This is an advantage for Way of the Horse, but means Butterfly has no effect at all.)
If you gain this onto your deck (with e.g. {card:Armory}), you didn't gain it to your discard pile, so Night Watchman's ability doesn't trigger and it stays on your deck.

If you happen to put a card on top of your deck in the middle of resolving Night Watchman—for instance, by discarding a {card:Tunnel}, gaining a {card:Gold}, and top-decking it due to {card:Progress}—then when you return any remaining cards to your deck they will go on top of the card you just put there.
Noble Brigand is an Attack card, and when you announce it, players can use cards like {card:Moat} in response.
Because when-gain effects happen after when-buy effects, that means you can buy a Noble Brigand, do its attack, and then use {card:Trader} to get a {card:Silver} instead of keeping the Noble Brigand.
If you play the same Nobles multiple times, such as with {card:Throne Room}, {card:Procession}, or {card:King's Court}, you may make different choices for each play.
If you gain Nomad Camp but you exchange it (for e.g. a {card:Changeling}, the exchanged card goes in your discard pile, not on your deck.
If you gain this to your hand (with e.g. {card:Artisan}), you didn't gain it to your discard pile, so Nomad Camp's ability doesn't trigger and it stays in your hand.
An effect that tries to move Nomad Camp *after* it is gained (such as {card:Summon}) will successfully move it from your deck without losing track of it.

If you {card:Possession|Possess} a player and make them gain a Nomad Camp, you'll gain it onto your deck. This is in contrast to other ways to gain cards onto your deck (such as {card:Crafters' Guild}), in which case Possession will make you gain the card to your discard pile instead.
When you gain this in your Buy phase, getting the {coin:+2} will let you take {vp:2} from {card:Basilica}.
If you buy {card:Ball}, you take your -1 Coin token, and then if you gain a Nomads, the {coin:+2} will be reduced to {coin:+1}.

If the chosen Action card is also a Victory card, they will be worth an additional {vp:2}. This means that {card:Great Hall} and {card:Mill} are worth {vp:3}, while {card:Dame Josephine}, {card:Island} and {card:Nobles} are now worth {vp:4}.
A player who is unaffected by Old Witch, such as due to {card:Moat}, neither gains a Curse nor may trash one.
The Curse is gained before you may trash one. So you can gain a Curse, react with {card:Sheepdog}, draw a Curse, and then trash that Curse.
Although in most cases, the order you put your 2 cards back won't matter, it does matter when you aren't drawing 2 cards (either because of your -1 Card token, or {card:Way of the Chameleon}).
Note that {card:Emissary} and {card:Underling} can cause you to shuffle before giving you Favors; the Favors you don't have yet can't be used on that shuffle.
If you shuffle your entire deck (with e.g. {card:Inn}), you may still spend Favors for Order of Astrologers. If you do, you get to look through your entire deck.
If you have {card:Star Chart}, you may pick one card to go on top for free, and then may spend Favors to put additional cards on top.

If you spend multiple Favors for this, you can choose the order for the cards you put on top of the shuffled cards. This may matter if e.g. you play {card:Smithy} with 2 cards in your deck, and the Smithy will only draw one of the cards you put on top with Order of Astrologers.

The cards you choose with this go on top of the other shuffled cards, not on top of your deck. So if you play Smithy with 2 {card:Town|Towns} in your deck, you can't use Order of Astrologers to put 3 {card:Copper|Coppers} on top of the Towns; you're forced to draw those 2 Towns dead.
You can't look through your cards unless you spend at least one Favor. You can look at any to-be-drawn cards while making this decision, as with {card:Order of Astrologers}.
Note that {card:Emissary} and {card:Underling} can cause you to shuffle before giving you Favors; the Favors you don't have yet can't be used on that shuffle.
Putting cards into your discard pile doesn't count as discarding (e.g. it won't activate e.g. {card:Village Green}).
If you have {card:Star Chart}, you can both choose a card to go on top of of the shuffle, and spend Favors to leave cards in your discard pile.
When you shuffle your entire deck (with e.g. {card:Inn} or {card:Famine}), you may spend Favors to both look through your entire deck, and put cards directly into your discard pile.

When you need to shuffle to access more cards from your deck, you only shuffle one time, even if Order of Masons put some cards back in your discard pile. For example, if {card:Sentinel} makes you shuffle a discard pile of 2 {card:Curse|Curses} and 2 {card:Province|Provinces}, but you spend a Favor to leave the 2 Provinces in your discard pile, the Sentinel will only look at the 2 Curses; you won't shuffle a 2nd time for the 2 Provinces.

However, some cards access cards from your deck one at a time (e.g. {card:Watchtower} and {card:Journeyman}). If there aren't enough cards after shuffling for the first time, you will shuffle a second time.
If for example you play {card:Merchant Ship} and Outpost on the same turn, then the extra turn will be your next turn, and you'll get {coin:+2} from Merchant Ship then.
With {card:Fleet}, you can take extra turns after the normal game end, but not after the final Fleet turn.
If you play Outpost multiple times with a card like Throne Room, {card:Throne Room} stays in play with Outpost even though you won't get a second extra turn.

You can't be sure Outpost will fail until you are in between turns, determining what turn happens next. If Outpost fails, or its turn is skipped by {card:Lich}, you discard it during Clean-up of the next turn, whoever's turn it is.

For example, if you play Outpost and {card:Voyage}, then in Clean-up you don't discard either of them and only draw 3 cards. In between turns, you choose to take the Voyage turn next. (Outpost hasn't failed yet because another player might somehow be able to take an extra turn first.) In Clean-up of the Voyage turn, you discard Voyage but not Outpost and draw 5 cards. In between turns again, Outpost now fails - it is up next but would be your 3rd turn in a row. The next player takes their turn and during their Clean-up, you discard Outpost.
For example if you use {card:Altar} to trash Overgrown Estate, you first draw a card, then gain a card costing up to {cost:5}.
If an Overgrown Estate is revealed when playing {card:Ambassador}, it is not returned to the Supply (since it is not in the Supply) and opponents do not gain a copy of it.

If you buy a {card:Farmland} and trash an Overgrown Estate, you immediately draw a card. However, even if the drawn card is a Treasure, you are unable to play it since you must play all Treasures before you buy a card.
The played Action card stays in the Supply; if an effect tries to move it, such as {card:Encampment} trying to set itself aside, it will fail to move it.
Since the played card is not in play, "while this is in play" abilities (like on {card:Groundskeeper}†) will not do anything.

Leave Overlord in play until the Clean-up of the turn the card it played would have left play. Normally that means you'll discard it that turn, but if Overlord plays {card:Crown} which in turn plays a Duration card several times, Overlord will stay out with the Duration card as Crown would have.

 Cards {card:Urchin} and {card:Goons}, however, may persist as valid examples.
Overlord plays similarly to {card:Band of Misfits}, so see the other rules clarifications there.

This only checks how many piles are empty when you play it; how many +Actions you got does not change if a pile becomes empty later in the turn (or non-empty, such as due to {card:Ambassador} from Seaside).
This only counts Supply piles, not non-Supply piles like {card:Horse}.
If gaining the Horses empties a Supply pile (e.g. you exchange them for a {card:Changeling}, which then empties the Changeling pile), you will get +1 Action for that pile.
When you discard it from play, you may return it to its pile and take a {card:Treasure Hunter}, putting it into your discard pile.
If you have {cost:2} unspent, you can discard a {card:Wine Merchant} from your Tavern mat, and then pay {cost:1} for Pageant.
If your turn has multiple Buy phases (due to {card:Villa} or {card:Cavalry}), you can pay {cost:1} to Pageant at the end of each of those Buy phases.
This applies even to Action-Treasures that are played during the Action phase, such as {card:Crown} or Actions under the influence of {card:Capitalism}.
{card:Jewels} is never discarded from play, so it does not get returned to its pile.
If this plays a card that can't normally be played, like {card:Territory} (from Allies), that card goes into play but doesn't do anything else then.

If you have multiple Patient cards with different names, you can play them in any order. So if you set aside {card:Sunken Treasure} and {card:Distant Shore}, you can first play Sunken Treasure, gain a Distant Shore, then play the set-aside Distant Shore.
If Patient cards get put into your hand at the start of Clean-up (e.g. you trash a Patient {card:Fortress} with {card:Improve}), you may set it aside to play it at the start of your next turn.
Cards costing {debt:} do not cost {cost:5} or more unless they also have a {cost:} cost of {cost:5} or more. So {card:Fortune} does but {card:City Quarter} does not.
For example if you play a {card:Border Guard} and reveal two Patrons, you will get +2 Coffers.
Other players seeing a card, without the word "reveal" being used, is not enough; for example if another player plays a {card:Villain} and you discard a Patron, you do not get +1 Coffers.
If you play {card:Black Market} and Patron is one of the 3 cards revealed from the Black Market deck, you get +1 Coffers.
If you have {card:Capitalism}, you may discard Patron to {card:Hostelry}. If you do, you will reveal the Patron for +1 Coffers.

Patron only gives Coffers during an Action phase. It doesn't have to be *your* Action phase, but it won't give Coffers if revealed during the Buy phase by, for example, an Event such as {card:Pursue}.
If Pawn is played multiple times (for example with {card:Throne Room}), the choices do not have to be the same for each play of Pawn.

If trashing those cards gets you more Favors (e.g. by trashing a {card:Sycophant}) or more cards in your hand (e.g. by trashing a {card:Cultist}), you won't be able to trash more cards with Peaceful Cult.
If you take multiple Buy phases in a turn (with e.g. {card:Villa} or {card:Cavalry}), you can trash with Peaceful Cult multiple times a turn.
When you discard it from play, you may return it to its pile and take a {card:Soldier}, putting it into your discard pile.
If you play {card:King's Court} on {card:Worker's Village}, for example, that's just two Action cards you have in play, even though you played the Worker's Village three times.
Buying cards using the promotional card {card:Black Market} is something that does not happen during a Buy phase, so Peddler still costs {cost:8} then.

During your Buy phase, if you get more Action cards into your play area (with e.g. {card:Toil}), Peddler's cost will be further reduced. And if any Action cards leave your play area (e.g. you {card:Scepter} a card and play it as {card:Way of the Butterfly}), Peddler's cost will increase.
{card:Crown} is an Action card, even if you play it as a Treasure in the Buy phase, and so playing it in the Buy phase affects Peddler's cost.

When an Action is played during the Buy phase, Peddler's cost changes as soon as the new card enters your play area. So if you have 1 Action in play and then play a {card:Workshop} (with e.g. {card:Toil}), Peddler now costs {cost:4}, and can be gained by Workshop's effect.

Unlike {card:Destrier}, this changes cost only during your Buy phase. So if you return to your Action phase (with e.g. {card:Villa} or {card:Cavalry}), or enter your Night and/or Clean-up phase, Peddler will return to its normal cost of {cost:8}.
This counts itself. For example if you had three {card:Copper|Coppers}, a {card:Gondola} played last turn, and the Pendant in play, it would make {coin:+3}.

It is sometimes possible to play multiple copies of Philosopher's Stone that give different amounts of {cost:}. For example, if you have 20 cards in your deck and play this, it produces {cost:4}. Then, you could play a {card:Crystal Ball} (from Prosperity), which could cause you to reveal and play another copy of this. When you play the second copy, you would only have 19 cards in your deck, so it would only produce {cost:3}.
It does not matter what turned over the Journey token; you could turn it face down with {card:Ranger}, then face up with Pilgrimage.
You cannot gain copies of cards that are not from the Supply, such as {card:Mercenary} or {card:Disciple}.
Then, if you did, you gain two {card:Spoils} cards.†
If you have {card:Capitalism}, gaining an Action with {coin:+} in its text will let all players play Pirates from their hand.
Players revealing a card like {card:Moat} do so before you choose your option.
In games using Pixie, replace one of your starting {card:Copper|Coppers} with a {card:Goat}.

Even though you can only put the Trashing token on an Action Supply pile, the card you gain from the pile doesn't need to be an Action. So if you put your Trashing token on the {card:Odysseys} and then gain a {card:Sunken Treasure}, you may still trash a card from your hand.
You can trash with Plan even if you gain a card on another player's turn (e.g. with {card:Messenger} or {card:Falconer}).

"From that pile" is referring to the pile that the gained card started in, not where you gained the card from. So if you put your Trashing token on a card, and then gain a copy of it from the trash (with e.g. {card:Lurker}), you'll get to trash a card.
For example, if you have five Favors, two {card:Estate|Estates}, and a {card:Moat}, you can make three pairs, for {vp:6}.
Cards must cost exactly {cost:2} to count, which means that {card:Apothecary} can't be paired with a Favor.

Most forms of cost reduction (e.g. {card:Bridge}) have no effect when scoring. However, {card:Cheap} cards still cost {cost:1} less when scoring, which may matter for Plateau Shepherds, and {card:Flourishing Trade} remains in effect, which definitely matters.
Non-Supply piles, such as {card:Spoils}, do not matter to Poacher.
In games using Pooka, replace one of your starting {card:Copper|Coppers} with a {card:Cursed Gold}.
You gain the top card from each Action pile in the Supply; you do not gain non-Supply cards like {card:Horse}, or non-Action cards like {card:Stockpile}.
If there are different cards in an Action pile, like the {card:Knights} (from Dark Ages), you just get the top one.
For piles with different cards, the pile is an Action pile if the randomizer is an Action; so, {card:Castles} (from Empires) are not one.
If you gain {card:Cavalry} or {card:Villa} (from Empires) with Populate, you return to your Action phase right then, but still finish gaining cards from Populate before doing more things.
If you have bought {card:Inheritance}, {card:Estate|Estates} will be Action cards, but Populate won't gain an Estate, because the Estate pile is still a Victory pile.
Similarly, if {card:Enlightenment} is active, it will not affect which cards are gained by Populate, as only card types are effected, not pile types.

Populate gains you the top card of an Action Supply pile, even if the current top card isn't an Action (e.g. it's {card:Fortune} or {card:Territory}). You can check the types of a kingdom pile by checking its randomizer.

In the unusual event that new piles are added to the Supply while Populate is being resolved (e.g., Populate gains you an Omen, you play the Omen immediately using {card:Innovation}, and doing so activates {card:Divine Wind}), you gain from the new Supply piles too.

You can see the Possessed player's cards for the entire turn, which means you will see their next hand during Clean-up. You will also see any cards they are entitled to see due to card rules; for example you can look at cards they have set aside with {card:Native Village} (from Dominion: Seaside).

During the Possessed turn, whenever one of that player's cards is trashed, set it aside, and that player puts it into their discard pile at the end of the turn, after Clean-up. The card is still trashed, so for example you could have them trash a {card:Mining Village} (from Dominion: Intrigue) and get the {coin:+2}. Getting those cards back at end of turn does not count as those cards being gained (so for example, you will not get them). Other players' cards that are trashed during that turn are not returned.

Cards passed with {card:Masquerade} (from Dominion: Intrigue) are not being gained or trashed. Exchanging a card (such as {card:Soldier} from Adventures) does not count as gaining or trashing. Cards returned to the Supply, such as with {card:Swap} (from Dominion: Allies) are also not being trashed, and so return to the Supply normally.

If you make another player play an Attack via Possession, that Attack will hit you like it would normally. If you want to use a Reaction in response to that Attack (such as {card:Moat}), you would be the one revealing the Reaction, not the player being Possessed.

Possession causes an extra turn to be played, like the card {card:Outpost} does (from Dominion: Seaside). The extra turn happens only after this turn is completely over - you will have discarded everything and drawn your next hand. Outpost only prevents itself from giving a player two consecutive turns, it does not prevent other cards or the rules from doing so. So for example if you play Possession in a two-player game, then after the Possession turn, that player still gets their normal turn. If they played Outpost during that turn though, it would not give them an extra turn (unless another player took a turn in between, such as via another Possession). If you play both Outpost and Possession in the same turn, the Outpost turn happens first. If you make someone play Outpost during a turn in which you Possessed them, that player will get the extra turn and make decisions during it and so forth, not you; if you make someone play Possession during a turn in which you Possessed them, that will make that player Possess the player to their left, rather than you getting to Possess anyone further. Possession turns (and other extra turns) do not count for the tiebreaker. Once the game ends, no further turns are played, including extra turns from Possession and Outpost.
You get the benefit of "when you gain this" abilities. For example, if you make them buy a {card:Spices}, you gain it so you get the +2 Coffers.
You gain the card, but you did not buy it, so you would not e.g. gain a {card:Curse} from another player's {card:Swamp Hag}.

Gainers with abilities based on what they gain won't do anything because the player didn't gain a card. For example, if you have them play {card:Replace} to trash a {card:Gold} and you gain a {card:Province}, no one gains Curses because *they* didn't gain a Victory card.
They don't gain any cards, so abilities like {card:Cauldron} will never trigger.
If you gain a card like {card:Den of Sin} that says it goes somewhere instead of your discard pile, it still goes there.
If you play a card like {card:Black Cat} during their Possession turn, you gain the Curse they would have gained.
Cards trashed on a Possession turn are set aside, so they are not in the trash for cards like {card:Graverobber} or {card:Necromancer}.
If you have a player trash a {card:Fortress} during their Possession turn, you choose whether they put it into their hand or set it aside.
Between playing each of the set-aside cards, you cannot play any cards from your hand, unless a card specifically tells you so (for example, {card:Throne Room}).
This is cumulative, even if the same Priest is played multiple times (such as with {card:Scepter}).

The bonus works even if the card was not trashed from your hand; for example you will get {coin:+2} for trashing an {card:Acting Troupe} due to playing it, or for trashing a card from the Supply with {card:Lurker} (from Intrigue).
With {card:Sewers}, the extra trashing from Sewers happens before the "For the rest of the turn" ability happens, so you don't get {coin:+2} for that trash.
If you use {card:Way of the Chameleon} on Priest, then every {coin:+2} it gives you is replaced by +2 Cards for the rest of the turn.
For example, if you set aside a {card:Village}, you will get +1 Card and +2 Actions at the start of each of your turns.

The Action card stays set aside. If the card tries to move itself (e.g. {card:Mining Village}), it stays set aside and it fails to move. If the card has a bonus that is conditional on moving itself (such as {card:Pixie}, which gives Boons only if it trashes itself), you won't get its bonus. But if the bonus is not phrased so as to be conditional on the card moving (such as {card:Acting Troupe}, which trashes itself and gives you Villagers), you'll get its bonus.
Prince plays its Action on extra turns from {card:Outpost}, {card:Possession}, etc.

If you play this with {card:Throne Room}, you can set aside 2 cards on this. You will play both of them at the start of each of your turns. Both the Throne Room and the Prince will stay in play for the rest of the game.
If you play a {card:Necromancer} that plays a Throne Room that plays a Prince twice, the Necromancer will stay in play for the rest of the game.
However, if you play a Prince via an effect triggered by the start of your turn (e.g. with {card:Piazza}) and set aside a card, you'll play the set-aside card on the same turn.
The start of your turn is part of your Action phase. This matters if you use Prince to play {card:Crown}.
For example if you played Princess, then {card:Remake}, trashing a {card:Copper}, you could gain a {card:Silver}, as Silver would cost {cost:1} while Copper would still cost {cost:0}.

This is cumulative with itself and with other forms of cost reduction: for instance, if you play a {card:Bridge} and then Princess, costs will be reduced by a total of {cost:3}; if you use {card:Throne Room} on a Princess, costs will be reduced by {cost:4}
If something happens due to trashing the card - for example drawing three cards due to trashing a {card:Cultist} - that will resolve before you gain a card.
This does not use up any extra Actions you were allowed to play due to cards like {card:Fortress} - Procession itself uses up one Action and that is it.
If you Procession a card that gives you +1 Action, such as {card:Vagrant}, you will end up with two Actions to use afterwards, rather than the one you would have left if you just played two Vagrants.

If you play Procession on a one-shot card, the stop-moving rule applies and the one-shot will end up where it instructs you to put it. For example, if you use Procession on {card:Horse}, the Horse is played, returning itself to its pile, then is played a second time, and then Procession tries and fails to trash it because it has already been moved. The Horse does not end up in the trash, but you still gain a {cost:4} Action since Procession's gaining is not conditional on the Horse being trashed. Similarly, if you play Procession on an {card:Island}, the Island is set aside on its mat and is not trashed by Procession, and you gain a {cost:5} Action anyway.
Similarly, Reserve cards such as {card:Guide} also are not trashed by Procession, since they move themselves to the Tavern mat when played; and you gain a more expensive Action anyway.
This also applies to cards that would normally be gained to unusual locations, such as a {card:Den of Sin} or anything gained with {card:Blockade}.

However, the stop-moving rule can in some cases prevent a card from being placed on your deck. For instance, you may use a {card:Sleigh} to move a gained card into your hand; if you do, Progress will no longer be able to move it onto your deck.

You may have to read card texts carefully to determine whether something is gained directly to an unusual location (in which case Progress overrules it) or is moved after being gained (so the stop-moving rule can apply). For instance, although {card:Ghost Town} and {card:Villa} may appear similar in their gaining behavior, Ghost Town is gained *to* the hand (and must be moved to the deck by Progress), whereas Villa moves itself to the hand *after* being gained (which can overrule Progress).

For example in a game with {card:Gondola}, you might choose to gain Gondola, resolve its "when gain" ability to play a {card:Trickster}, then choose to gain a {card:Gold} and a {card:Silver} and then stop.

Unlike {card:Populate}, this checks the types of a card and not the types of a pile. This is why Populate cannot gain an {card:Estate} that's been affected by {card:Inheritance}, but Prosper can gain a {card:Curse} that's been affected by {card:Charlatan}, or an Action that's been affected by {card:Capitalism}.
Prosper can potentially gain multiple cards from the same pile. For example, if you have Capitalism, you can gain a {card:Tent}, revealing a {card:Garrison} that you can now gain.
This is cumulative; if you play two Quarries in your Buy phase, then {card:King's Court} will only cost {cost:3}, rather than the usual {cost:7}.
If you play this twice with e.g. {card:Tiara} or {card:Crown}, costs will be reduced by {cost:4}, to a minimum of {cost:0}.

If you play two Quartermasters, they each have their own set of cards. However if you {card:Throne Room} a Quartermaster, you just have one set of cards for it, and twice on each of your turns, either add one or take one.
The card you gain is immediately set aside, and doesn't visit your discard pile. So if you gain a {card:Ghost Town}, it will be set aside on this (instead of going to your hand).

However, abilities that move cards *when you gain them* can move a card that's gained with Quartermaster. So if you gain a {card:Siren} with this, it will still trash itself (unless you trash an Action from your hand).
Night cards are not Treasures or Actions (except {card:Werewolf}), so they are not discarded by the attack.
This Event is like an Attack, but buying it is not playing an Attack, and so cannot be responded to with cards like {card:Moat} and {card:Caravan Guard}.
It does not matter what turned over the Journey token; you could turn it face down with {card:Giant}, then face up with Ranger.

This even applies to cards that would ordinarily be gained directly to your hand for immediate use. For instance, if you use {card:Mine} while Rapid Expansion is in effect, the gained Treasure will be set aside and can't be played on the current turn.

The stop-moving rule can in some cases allow you to interrupt Rapid Expansion's effect. For instance, if you gain a {card:Villa} while Rapid Expansion is in effect, you get two competing "when you gain this" movement instructions: Villa telling you to put it in your hand, and Rapid Expansion telling you to set it aside. Since these two instructions activate at the same time, you can choose which one to follow first (and then the other will be blocked by the stop-moving rule). However, this doesn't apply in the case of cards such as {card:Mine} (see above) because of the No Visiting rule: in the case of Mine, the Treasure is gained directly to your hand, rather than moved to your hand at a time that conflicts with Rapid Expansion.
Costs may be affected by cards like {card:Bridge Troll}.

Just like Ways, if a Reckless card is affected by {card:Enchantress} and/or {card:Highwayman}, you won't do its instructions twice, and you still return the Reckless card to its pile when discarding it from play.

The exception is {card:Way of the Chameleon}, which tells you to "follow this card's instructions." So if you play a Reckless card as Way of the Chameleon, you'll follow its instructions twice, switching +Cards and {coin:+} both times.
Even though you follow a Reckless card's instructions twice, that only counts as 1 card played (which matters for e.g. {card:Conspirator}).

Some cards care if it's the 1st time you played a copy of it this turn; if it's Reckless, both iterations will be the 1st time you played it. So your 1st Reckless {card:Fool's Gold} gives {coin:+2}, and your 1st Reckless {card:Crossroads} gives +6 Actions.

Both iterations will count as something the card did. So if you play a {card:Harbor Village}, then play a Reckless {card:Steward} and choose +2 Cards and {coin:+2}, that will let {card:Harbor Village} give {coin:+1}.
Abilities that happen *after* playing a card (e.g. {card:Frigate} or {card:Landing Party}) are resolved (once) after you finish both iterations of a Reckless card.

If a Reckless card is an Attack, a single {card:Shield} reveal (which you have to reveal before the first iteration of the Reckless card) will block both attacks (even if you want to get attacked the 2nd time).
If an attacked player draws a Shield as a result of the 1st attack (e.g. the attack was {card:Soothsayer}), they don't get to reveal the Shield against the 2nd attack.

If a Reckless card never gets discarded from play (e.g. {card:Quartermaster}, {card:Search}, or a one-shot), you'll follow its instructions twice, but you'll never return it to its pile (so there's effectively no downside).
If another card moves a Reckless card when it's discarded from play (e.g. {card:Scheme}), it'll fail to return to its pile.

If {card:Divine Wind} goes into effect, removing the Reckless pile from the supply, you still follow the cards' instructions twice, but you can't return them to the removed pile, so they get discarded as usual.
Relic is an Attack despite not being an Action; it can be blocked with {card:Moat} and responded to with {card:Caravan Guard} and so on.

This is in contrast to other cards that trash multiple cards at once (like {card:Count}). Even though Remake trashes 2 cards, the trashes take place one after another, instead of all at once. This means you can use Remake to trash the same {card:Fortress} twice, which is not possible with other two-card trashers such as {card:Steward}.
For example if you play Renown and then {card:Remake}, trashing a {card:Copper}, you could gain a {card:Silver}, as Silver would cost {cost:1} while Copper would still cost {cost:0}.
Using a card like {card:Throne Room} on Renown will make cards cost {cost:4} less.
Like {card:Remodel}, you first trash a card from your hand, then gain a card from the Supply costing up to {cost:2} more than the trashed card, putting the gained card into your discard pile.
It is possible to get both bonuses; if you gain {card:Harem}, {card:Mill}, or {card:Nobles} with Replace, it both goes on your deck and causes the other players to each gain a Curse.

Replace is *not* subject to the no visiting rule. If you gain an Action or Treasure with Replace, it is first gained to your discard pile (or whatever its default gain location is), and then it is moved to the top of your deck if possible. If an on-gain effect causes it to be moved elsewhere first, Replace will fail to topdeck it. So for example, if you gain an Action card and then use {card:Innovation} on it, Replace cannot remove the card from your play area and put it onto your deck.

Replace will also fail to move a card if it moves away, and then moves back to the same place. For example, if you gain an {card:Experiment}, Exile it with {card:Gatekeeper}, then gain the second Experiment and discard the first Experiment from Exile, Replace will still fail to topdeck the Experiment, even though it's still in your discard pile.

For example, if you had a {card:Daimyo}, a {card:Litter}, a {card:Fishmonger}, three {card:Copper|Coppers}, and Rice in play, the types would be Action, Command, Shadow, and Treasure, so Rice would make {coin:+4}.

Ritual cares about the cost of the card after it has been trashed. For example, if you trash a {card:Wayfarer} (which costs {cost:0} from the {card:Curse}), then discard a {card:Market Square} to gain a {card:Gold}, Ritual will give {vp:6} and not {vp:0} since {card:Wayfarer} now costs {cost:6}.
If you have multiple Buy phases, such as via {card:Continue}, River Shrine only gains you a card if you didn't gain a card in any of those Buy phases.

If this gains a 2nd River Shrine and you play it with {card:Rush}, that River Shrine will also gain a card.

Riverboat is normally discarded in your next turn's Clean-up, but it stays in play as long as the card it plays would have, which sometimes is longer (such as a {card:Crown}, from Empires, used on a Duration card).
This can't choose non-Supply cards that cost {cost:5} (like {card:Disciple}).
This can choose {cost:5}'s in a split pile (like {card:Bustling Village}).
