The chosen card does not have a pile, which means that if it's {card:Wild Hunt}, it can't gather {vp:}.
Unlike {card:Band of Misfits}, Riverboat is not a Command card.

Rogue is an Attack card, even when it is gaining cards from the trash rather than putting opponents' cards in the trash, and so an opponent can reveal a Reaction such as {card:Diplomat} when you play it even if it's not attacking them at the time.
Royal Carriage cannot respond to Actions that are no longer in play, such as a Reserve card that was put on the Tavern mat, or a card that trashed itself (like a {card:Raze} used to trash itself).

With Duration cards, you call Royal Carriage after resolving the Duration card's on-play effects; you don't wait for the next turn. The same applies to other cards that have delayed effects, such as {card:Scheme}.
Royal Carriage can be called on a {card:Crown} or {card:Coronet} played during your Buy phase, and on a {card:Werewolf} played during your Night phase.

You can also call Royal Carriage on a card you play on another player's turn (e.g. {card:Caravan Guard} or {card:Falconer}). If it's a Duration, Royal Carriage will stay in play; otherwise you will discard the Royal Carriage during that player's Clean-up.

If a card you play leaves and then immediately returns to your play area (e.g. you play a {card:Transmogrify} at the start of your turn with {card:Piazza} and then immediately call the Transmogrify), you can't call Royal Carriage on it.
If an Action card, such as {card:Disciple}, plays a Royal Carriage, you can immediately (after completely resolving Disciple) call the Royal Carriage to replay the Disciple.

If an Action plays another Action (such as a {card:Sauna} that plays an {card:Avanto}), you will call Royal Carriages in the opposite order of when they were played. So you can't call Royal Carriage on Sauna before Avanto. If you call a Royal Carriage on Sauna, you can no longer call Royal Carriage on Avanto.

If an Action is in play, and you replay it with a Royal Carriage to remove it from play (e.g. you replay a {card:Tragic Hero} and it trashes itself, then you can no longer call other Royal Carriages on it.
If you have 3 Favors, play an {card:Underling}, and then replay it with Royal Carriage, {card:League of Shopkeepers} will trigger twice, and you can get {coin:+2} from it.
If you Royal Galley a Throne Room, and on your next turn, you make the Throne Room play a Duration (like {card:Caravan}), the Throne Room stays in play, but Royal Galley doesn't.
This applies both to cards gained due to being bought, and to cards gained other ways with Royal Seal in play, such as with {card:Hoard}.
If Royal Seal is no longer in play when you gain a card, such as because it was trashed with {card:Mint} or top-decked with {card:Mandarin}, you cannot use its ability.
Costs of cards are affected by {card:Bridge}.
{card:The Field's Gift} and {card:The Forest's Gift} are not shared.
{card:The River's Gift} means that each player choosing to receive it draws a card at the end of your turn, at the same time as you.
If you trash a card with multiple types, you get all relevant bonuses; for example if you trash {card:Crown}, you get +2 Cards, +2 Actions, and {coin:+2}.
Sacrificing an {card:Estate} under the influence of {card:Inheritance} will give +2 Cards, +2 Actions, and {vp:+2}.
Sailor applies to cards gained due to being bought, or gained other ways, such as with {card:Workshop}.
The Duration doesn't need to be an Action; you can also play Night-Durations and Treasure-Durations when you gain them (like {card:Cobbler} and {card:Astrolabe}).
If you exchange a {card:Hero} for a {card:Champion}, you aren't gaining it, so you can't play it.
If you gain a {card:Garrison} and play it, you'll immediately add a token to Garrison.

This can play a gained Duration even if it was gained to somewhere other than your discard pile (such as a {card:Guardian}, or a card gained with {card:Blockade}), or if another card is trying to move it at the same time (such as {card:Gatekeeper}). But if the gained card has already gotten moved (e.g. by another Sailor), then this can't play it.
If the trashed card does something when trashed (such as {card:Crumbling Castle}), you do that thing.
Putting your deck into your discard pile will not trigger cards that do something when discarded, such as {card:Tunnel} (from Hinterlands).
Scepter can replay an Action that isn't finished resolving, such as a {card:Storyteller} that played Scepter in the first place.
If a card you play leaves and then later returns to your play area (for example, if you play a {card:Duplicate} and then call it on the same turn), you can't replay it with Scepter.
If a Duration card has been played for both a non-Duration ability (such as {card:Barge}, or a Way) and a next-turn effect, the Scepter will stay in play, since the Action card is staying in play.
Scheme is cumulative; if you play two Schemes, or {card:Throne Room} a Scheme, you will be able to put up to two discarded Action cards onto your deck, and so on.

Scheme still has its Clean-up effect even if it is no longer in play by the time you start your Clean-up phase; specifically, if you play {card:Procession} on Scheme, at the start of Clean-up you will be able to put two Action cards from play on top of your deck, even though your Scheme has already been trashed and will not be in play itself.

You discard all cards in your hand at once, then activate any abilities triggered by the discard one at a time, and then draw seven cards. For instance, if your hand includes two {card:Trail}s, you discard both of them, allowing you play the Trails for +1 card each, and then draw 7 more cards, for a total new hand of nine cards.

If you happen to put a card on top of your deck in the middle of resolving Scouting Party—for instance, by discarding a {card:Tunnel}, gaining a {card:Gold}, and top-decking it due to {card:Progress}—then when you return the remaining cards to your deck they will go on top of the card you just put there.
So you might trash an {card:Estate}, choose +1 Card and "gain a {card:Horse}," then draw a card and then gain the Horse.

If you choose +1 Card as well as "gain a {card:Silver}" and/or "gain a Horse", and the card you draw is a Reaction that reacts to a card being gained, such as {card:Sheepdog}, you can use the Reaction ability to react to the gain.
If you gain a {card:Nomad Camp} (from Hinterlands) with this, it goes to your hand.
If you {card:Throne Room} a Search, Throne Room will stay out with Search until a pile empties, and then you'll trash Search once but gain two Loots (and discard Throne Room that turn).

It doesn't matter if the Supply pile had already been emptied on a previous turn. So if you empty a pile, return copies to the Supply (with e.g. {card:Swap}), and empty it again, Search can trigger off that pile again.
If a non-supply pile (like Loot or {card:Horse}) is emptied, that won't trigger Search.

If gaining a card empties a Supply pile, you'll order Search with other when-gain effects. If trashing a card empties a Supply pile (e.g. {card:Lurker}), you'll order Search with other when-trash effects.
If you {card:Invest} in the last card of a Supply pile, other players who also Invested in that card can order between the +2 Cards from Invest and trashing their Searches.

If emptying a Supply pile causes you to play this (e.g. you gain the last {card:Gondola} which lets you play a Search), that won't trigger the Search (it triggers off the next Supply pile that's emptied).

Ending the game by emptying the third Supply pile, {card:Province|Provinces}, or {card:Colony|Colonies} does trigger Search; you gain the Loot before the game ends. Usually this won't make a difference, but trashing Search and gaining Loot can affect your score due to abilities such as {card:Fairgrounds}, {card:Tomb}, and {card:Keep}, and there are a few abilities that might allow you to play the gained Loot before the end of your final turn and use it to buy some additional {vp:}.

For example you can play {card:Bridge Troll}, then use Seaway to gain a Bridge Troll (currently costing {cost:4} due to its own effect), and the token will stay there even when Bridge Troll costs {cost:5} later.

You can use Seaway to gain {card:Sir Martin} (from Dark Ages) when he is on top of the Knights pile; then your +1 Buy token will be on the Knights pile, even though any remaining Knights will cost {cost:5}.

Unlike {card:Pathfinding}, {card:Lost Arts}, {card:Training}, and {card:Teacher}, Seaway doesn't require the pile to be an Action pile—just a pile you can gain an Action card from. This means (with cost-reduction), you can put the +1 Buy token on {card:Castles}. And with {card:Inheritance}, you can put the +1 Buy token on {card:Estate|Estates}.

The +1 Buy token is placed on the pile after the card has been gained and after any on-gain effects are resolved. This means if you gain a card with Seaway and then immediately play it with {card:Innovation}, the token isn't on the pile *yet*, so you won't get +1 Buy.
If you gain a {card:Gondola} and play a Secluded Shrine, that will trigger your other Secluded Shrines, but not the one you just played (it triggers off your *next* Treasure gain).
In games using Secret Cave, replace one of your starting {card:Copper|Coppers} with a {card:Magic Lamp}.

Revealing Secret Chamber happens prior to resolving what an Attack does to you. For example, if another player plays {card:Thief}, you can reveal Secret Chamber, draw 2 cards, put 2 back, and then you resolve getting hit by the Thief.

Also, you can reveal more than one Reaction card in response to an Attack. For example, after revealing the Secret Chamber in response to an Attack and resolving the effect of the Secret Chamber, you can still reveal a {card:Moat} to avoid the Attack completely.

You may reveal the same Secret Chamber multiple times when reacting to an Attack; for example, in response to an attack, you could reveal Secret Chamber, draw a {card:Moat} and a {card:Copper} off the top of your deck, put back two Coppers, reveal the Moat to be unaffected by the attack, and then reveal Secret Chamber again to put either the Moat or the Secret Chamber back on top of your deck.

Revealing the Secret Chamber alone does NOT prevent the attack from affecting you. You can reveal Secret Chamber even in response to an attack that does not affect the top of your deck, like {card:Witch}.

You must reveal the Secret Chamber as soon as the Attack is played, but before any text on it is resolved. So if your opponent plays {card:Minion} or {card:Pirate Ship}, you must finish drawing cards and then putting cards back on top before your opponent makes their choice for which action on attack card to take.

Unlike {card:Outpost} and {card:Mission}, Seize the Day doesn't check if the previous turn was another player's. So if you take an extra turn with {card:Outpost}, you can buy Seize the Day on the extra turn, and take a 3rd turn.

If you happen to put a card on top of your deck in the middle of resolving Sentry—for instance, by discarding a {card:Tunnel}, gaining a {card:Gold}, and top-decking it due to {card:Progress}—then when you return any remaining cards to your deck they will go on top of the card you just put there.

This works however you trash the card. For example it works when trashing a card to {card:Priest}, when trashing a {card:Curse} to {card:Old Witch}, when trashing {card:Acting Troupe} when playing it, and when trashing a card from the Supply with {card:Lurker} (from Intrigue).
When you trash multiple cards (with e.g. {card:Steward}), you trash them all at once, and then resolve any when-trashed abilities (which includes Sewers)

Just like {card:Monastery}, cards are trashed one at a time with Sewers. This matters if trashing one card (e.g., {card:Overgrown Estate}) causes you to draw another card; such cards drawn in the middle of trashing can be trashed by Sewers.

If you happen to put a card on top of your deck in the middle of resolving Sextant—for instance, by discarding a {card:Tunnel}, gaining a {card:Gold}, and top-decking it due to {card:Progress}—then when you return any remaining cards to your deck they will go on top of the card you just put there.
This applies even on your first turn (relevant with {card:Necromancer}, from Nocturne).
It's a card you gained, and can trigger things that care about that; for example gaining an {card:Estate} would trigger {card:Cage|Cage's} ability.
First resolve Shaman, gain nothing, and then trash a {card:Copper} with {card:Rope} (for the next player to gain).
First trash your {card:Cabin Boy} from play, and then gain it back from the trash with Shaman.
If it has no Action cards in it (including Action cards with other types too, such as {card:Nobles}), then you draw 2 cards.

If you {card:Throne Room} a Shanty Town, you reveal your hand, get +2 actions, and potentially draw two cards, then you reveal your hand again, get 2 more actions, and potentially draw two more cards. You do NOT reveal your hand once and get +4 cards.

You can use this when gaining a card due to buying it, when gaining a card some other way such as due to {card:Falconer}, and even when gaining a card on another player's turn, such as due to {card:Black Cat}.
If you gain a Sheepdog to your hand - such as via {card:Falconer} - you can react to that gain and play the Sheepdog.
If you gain a card that does something when you gain it (such as {card:Hostelry}), you can resolve that ability before or after Reacting with Sheepdog.
In games using Shepherd, replace one of your starting {card:Copper|Coppers} with a {card:Pasture}.
If drawing causes you to shuffle, you will shuffle in the discarded Victory cards. And if you discard a {card:Tunnel} and gain a {card:Gold}, the Gold will get shuffled in.
You can reveal this when another player plays an Attack card to be unaffected by it, exactly as with {card:Moat}.
This can gain {card:Silver}, but also other Treasures costing less than Silver Mine, when in the Supply: {card:Gondola}, {card:Jewelled Egg}, and so on.
Sir Martin only costs {cost:4}, though the other Knights all cost {cost:5}. When Sir Martin is the top card of the pile, it can be gained with an {card:Armory} and so on.

However if you manage to move the Siren from where it was gained (whether it was gained to your discard pile or somewhere else) before resolving this ability - for example putting it on top of your deck with {card:Insignia} - then it will fail to be trashed (though you can still trash an Action card if you want).
The important part of getting around Siren's self-trashing effect is to move it *when* it's gained. This is why {card:Insignia} works, but the following does not:
Some cards directly gain a card somewhere (e.g. {card:Invasion} gains an Action directly onto your deck). This does not actually move the Siren, so it will still trash itself.
A few other cards gain a card and then move it later. So if you gain a Siren with {card:Spell Scroll}, the Siren will trash itself, and the {card:Spell Scroll} will fail to play it.

If you have an Action in hand, you can decline to trash it, and let the Siren trash itself. This may still be useful if you want to trigger when-trash effects (such as {card:Sewers} or {card:Market Square}).
Revealing {card:Moat} when Skirmisher is played stops the attack; you can't reveal Moat when an Attack card is gained later.

You resolve all your on-gain abilities before the other players get to use their own on-gain abilities (assuming that it's your turn). This means that an attacked player has to discard to your Skirmisher first before they get to use {card:Invest} or {card:Falconer}.
If you gain Skirmisher and then play it (with e.g. {card:City-state}), the other players will discard down to 3 cards in hand.
When you gain an Attack, you may play it with City-state before attacking with Skirmisher. This may be useful if playing the Attack would draw them cards (such as {card:Soothsayer}).

If you gain a copy of Skirmisher with either {card:Disciple} or {card:Specialist}, Skirmisher will attack. But if you gain a copy of Skirmisher with {card:Kiln}, you won't attack, because you haven't followed Skirmisher's instructions yet.

Exchanging or exiling a card doesn't count as gaining it. So if you exchange a {card:Peasant} for a {card:Soldier}, or exile a Skirmisher with Invest, you won't attack. But if you gain an Attack and exchange it (e.g. for a {card:Changeling}), you'll still attack.

If you play multiple Skirmishers and then gain an Attack card, this means you will attack multiple times. So if your 1st Skirmisher attack makes them draw cards (e.g. they discard and play a {card:Trail}), your 2nd Skirmisher will once again make them discard down to 3 cards.
If a gained card goes directly to somewhere other than your discard pile (for example, the {card:Silver} gained from {card:Bureaucrat}), Sleigh can still move it to your hand or the top of your deck.

If you gain a Sleigh to your hand (with e.g. {card:Falconer}), you can use the Sleigh's Reaction to discard itself, but the stop-moving rule prevents you from then putting it back into your hand or onto your deck.
If you gain a {card:Cemetery}, you can React with a Sleigh to put it in your hand, and then trash the {card:Cemetery}.
This can only gain cards that are present in the Supply; for example you cannot gain a {card:Spoils} (from Dominion: Dark Ages).
This is not an Attack, so {card:Lighthouse} and {card:Moat} do not stop it.
It doesn't matter where the gained card came from. So if the player to your right gained a card from the trash with {card:Lurker}, you can gain a copy of that card (from the Supply).
If your opponent gained a Ruins or a {card:Knights|Knight}, Smugglers will only let you gain a copy if the top card of the Ruins or Knights pile has the same name.

If you play this during the player to your right's turn (e.g. they play {card:Barbarian}, trash your {card:Gold}, and you gain a {card:Gondola} that lets you play Smugglers), this checks that player's last completed turn, not their current turn.
Any extra Actions you already had before playing this do not go away; for example, if you play {card:Village} and then Snowy Village, you can play 5 more Actions after that.
This does not stop you from playing more cards via cards that tell you to play cards, such as {card:Throne Room}.

If you have played a {card:Champion}, you'll get +1 Action from it when you play Snowy Village, and then you won't get any +Actions from {card:Champion} for the rest of the turn. If {card:Great Leader} is in effect, Snowy Village similarly overrules the free +Actions it grants (including the one that it would try to give you after playing Snowy Village).
If you play this with {card:Conclave}, Snowy Village will prevent you from getting +1 Action from Conclave.

Soldier only cares about Attack cards in play, not Attack cards played that turn; for example using {card:Disciple} on Soldier will not produce an extra {coin:+1}, because there is no other Attack card in play.
A player who uses {card:Watchtower} (from Dominion: Prosperity) to trash the Curse did gain a Curse and so draws a card.
If you gain a Curse and draw a Reaction like {card:Sheepdog} or {card:Horse Traders}, it's too late to use it.
This card is not in the Supply; it can only be obtained via {card:Bandit Camp}, {card:Marauder}, and {card:Pillage}.

The official FAQ stipulation about how Spoils "can only be obtained" applies only to gaining it from its pile. If a Spoils is trashed, it can be gained from the trash via an ability like {card:Treasurer} or {card:Shaman}; and it can be obtained from another player's hand via {card:Masquerade}.
Spoils cannot be gained with {card:Mint}, since it is not in the Supply.
If you play an {card:Ambassador} and reveal a Spoils, the Spoils is not returned to the Supply (since it is not in the Supply) and other players do not gain Spoils.

In a strict interpretation of the rules, each player reveals their card and returns it or discards it before the next player does, and for certain cards (such as {card:Chariot Race}), this can matter when it comes to deciding which each player should do. However, in practice, it's usually fine for all players to reveal their cards at the same time for efficiency's sake, provided there's no effect in the game that cares about the order of revealing.
You cannot gain Attack cards that are not in the Supply by trashing a Squire, such as {card:Mercenary}, {card:Soldier}, or an Attack card set up by {card:Ferryman}.

It does not matter how many cards you played that turn, only how many you have in play when buying Stampede. If there are fewer than 5 {card:Horse|Horses} left in the pile, just gain as many as you can.
If you shuffle your entire deck (with e.g. {card:Famine}), you can look through your deck and pick a card to put on top.

If a card tells you to shuffle your entire deck, like {card:Inn} (from Dominion: Hinterlands), and Stash is in your deck, there is no "remaining deck" that isn't being shuffled, so you don't get to look at the front of any cards.
Because Stash has a different back, you'll be able to tell when it's in other players' hands, or set aside for a {card:Haven} (from Dominion: Seaside), and so on.
When you shuffle your entire deck (with e.g. {card:Annex}), you can reposition any Stashes in your deck. Any Stashes that you leave in your discard pile are not being shuffled.
Unlike {card:Order of Astrologers} (which doesn't let you spend Favors during setup), if Stash is {card:Inherited}, you can choose where it goes when you shuffle your starting deck.
If you play this twice with a card like {card:Crown} (from Empires), you will get {coin:+6} and +2 Buys total, even though you could only Exile it once.
If you play a Stockpile after a {card:Kiln}, you gain a Stockpile first, may discard Stockpiles from Exile, and then you Exile your played Stockpile.
If you gain a Stockpile and then play it (with {card:Mining Road}), you may discard your other Stockpiles from Exile, but you won't discard the one you just played.
The cards you gain are gained one at a time; this may matter with cards that do something when gained, such as {card:Inn} from Dominion: Hinterlands.
For example, if you buy Stonemason for {cost:6}, you could gain two {card:Herald|Heralds}.
You can't overpay with {debt:}, meaning you can't overpay by {debt:8} to gain 2 {card:City Quarter|City Quarters}.
To overpay and gain an {card:Animal Fair}, you have to overpay {cost:7}.
Stonemason is gained before any cards are gained through the overpay effect, meaning that {card:Wayfarer} will always cost {cost:2} even if it is the first of the two cards that you gain.

Cards gained through the on-play effect or overpay effect are chosen and gained separately. For example, if there is one {card:Crossroads} left in the pile, and you overpay by {cost:2} for Stonemason, you can't choose 2 Crossroads, then try to gain 2 Crossroads, failing to get the second one. You choose to gain 1 Crossroads, and then Crossroads is no longer an option for you to choose, forcing you to choose a different Action costing {cost:2} as your second gain.
The overpay effect will never let you gain 2 {card:Destrier|Destriers} as gaining the first one will, make Destrier no longer match the overpaid amount when it is time to gain the second card.

Treasures that have effects other than (or in addition to) giving you {coin:+} will still have their normal effects when played with Storyteller. For instance, {card:Quarry} will give you {coin:+1} and reduce the cost of Action cards; Storyteller will convert that {cost:1} into +1 Card, but the cost reduction will remain in effect.
Treasures that play other Treasures (such as {card:Counterfeit}, {card:Crystal Ball}, and {card:Tiara}) will let you play more than three Treasures while resolving Storyteller.

However, since under ordinary circumstances you'll be playing Storyteller in your Action phase, this means that playing {card:Crown} while resolving Storyteller will cause you to double-play another Action card, not an extra Treasure card.

Although Storyteller causes you to spend all your {cost:}, the Treasures that gave you that {cost:} remain in play. This means, for instance, that if you play {card:Copper} with Storyteller, you usually won't be able to buy {card:Grand Market} later in the turn.

Playing this with {card:Way of the Chameleon} means that will pay all your {cost:} just to get it back. This may still be useful just to get Treasures into play earlier than normal, without drawing any cards. Getting Treasures into play may be relevant for cards like {card:Quarry} and {card:Sea Chart}.
In 2022, Storyteller got errata that removed its {coin:+1}, and it instead gives you +1 Card after you play Treasures. Because of this change, Storyteller is no longer affected by {card:Capitalism}.

If you choose {coin:+3}, Stronghold will be discarded that turn; if you choose the +3 Cards next turn, Stronghold will stay out until that turn's Clean-up (and if you choose both via {card:Elder}, it will stay out).
If Student isn't in play (e.g. you played it from the Supply with {card:Band of Misfits}), trashing a Treasure means you'll get +1 Favor, but you won't put the Student on your deck.

If you {card:Throne Room} a Student and put it onto your deck, the Throne Room loses track of Student. And if you immediately draw the Student with {card:Fellowship of Scribes}, Throne Room can't move the Student back into play.

If you move the Action card after you gain it but before you set it aside (e.g. by putting it on top of your deck with {card:Watchtower} from Dominion: Prosperity), then Summon will "lose track" of it and be unable to set it aside; in that case you will not play it at the start of your next turn.

If you use Summon to gain a {card:Nomad Camp} (from the first edition of Dominion: Hinterlands), Summon will know to find the Nomad Camp on your deck, so you will set it aside in that case (unless you have moved it elsewhere via another ability).

If you are being {card:Possession|Possessed}, and the player to your right tells you to Summon a card, they gain the card, which does not get set aside, nor played at the start of their turn, instead staying in their discard pile.
If you Summon a {card:Hireling}, you will draw a card when you play it, since it will still be the start of your turn.

Summon will also fail to move a card if it moves away, and then moves back to the same place. For example, if you gain an {card:Experiment}, Exile it to {card:Gatekeeper}, then gain the second Experiment and discard the first Experiment from Exile, Summon will still fail to set aside the Experiment, even though it's still in your discard pile.
When you play this, gain a {card:Horse}, putting it directly onto your deck.
This does not affect cards gained other ways, only bought cards; for example using {card:Alms} to gain a {card:Silver} does not trigger this.

If you play Swamp Hag and then take an extra turn immediately, such as with {card:Mission}, you will get {coin:+3} at the start of that turn and discard Swamp Hag that turn, and other players will never be affected by it.
If you want to use a Reaction card like {card:Moat} against Swamp Hag, you have to use it right when Swamp Hag is played.
Buying a card via {card:Black Market} still causes a {card:Curse} to be gained, even though it usually takes place during the Action phase rather than the Buy phase.

Other when-gain effects happen at the same time as Swamp Hag's effects; the Attacked player chooses in which order to resolve them. This can matter, for instance, in the case of {card:Doctor|Doctor's} overpay, if it triggers a reshuffle.
It counts Treasures if you have some in play, such as Treasure Duration cards, or due to {card:Fortune Hunter}.
It does not count set aside cards, such as cards on a {card:Quartermaster}.

A non-Supply card (like {card:Horse} or cards gained with {card:Ferryman}) can be returned to its pile. However, a card with no pile (like {card:Necropolis}, or anything from the {card:Black Market} deck) can't be returned anywhere.

You can't gain a card that's not on top of its pile, which means you can't return a card and gain a card from the same pile. So if {card:Sorceress} is on top of the {card:Augurs} pile, and you return a {card:Herb Gatherer}, you can't gain the Sorceress because it's no longer on top.
If you {card:Possession|Possess} another player and make them Swap an Action card, their Action returns to its pile, and then you gain a differently named Action card to your discard pile.
If your discard pile has at least one card, you get +1 Coffers, and if you then have 4 or more tokens on your Coffers, you take the {card:Treasure Chest}.

Normally, if drawing the 3 cards would cause you to shuffle, you won't get a Coffers from this. But if you leave cards in your discard pile when shuffling (with {card:Order of Masons}), you'll get a Coffers from this.
If you take the Treasure Chest at the start of your Buy phase (e.g. by playing a Swashbuckler with {card:Market Towns}), you'll immediately gain a Gold.
This is an Attack, and so cards like {card:Moat} and {card:Shield} protect from it.
When you gain or trash this, you get +2 Favors; you can immediately spend them, for example on the ability of {card:City-state}.
If you use {card:Throne Room} on Tactician, you will discard your hand on the first play and will have no cards in hand for the second play (and so will not get the bonuses).
For example if you have two Talismans, four {card:Copper|Coppers}, and two Buys, you could buy {card:Silver} and {card:Trade Route}, gaining two more Silvers and two more Trade Routes.
Talisman only affects buying cards; it does not work on cards gained other ways, such as with {card:Expand}.

Talisman only cares about the cost of the card when you buy it, not its normal cost; so for example it can get you a {card:Peddler} if you have played two Actions this turn, thus lowering Peddler's cost to {cost:4}, or can get you a {card:Grand Market} if you have a {card:Quarry} in play.
When you buy a card from the {card:Black Market} deck, you do not get a second copy of it even if Talisman is in play, since there is no second copy in the Supply.

This checks the cost of a card when you buy it, even if it changes later. So if you buy a {card:Fisherman} for {cost:2} and then gain a {card:Sleigh} with {card:Charm}, you will gain a second {card:Fisherman}, even though it now costs {cost:5}.
When you play this, you trash a card from your hand, and gain a card costing up to {cost:2} more than it, like when playing {card:Remodel}.

Repeating Taskmaster's ability doesn't count as playing it again (which means you can't use a Way to make Taskmaster do something other than its usual ability at this point, and it won't count for {card:Conspirator}).
At the start of your turn, you can first repeat this ability, then gain a {card:Duchy} with {card:Importer}, and that will let the Taskmaster repeat itself on your next turn.

This checks the cost that a card had at the moment you gained it. So if you gain a {card:Destrier} that costs {cost:6}, that won't count for Taskmaster (even though its own gain means it now costs {cost:5}). But if you gain a Destrier that costs {cost:5} (meaning it now costs {cost:4}), that lets Taskmaster repeat itself.

If gaining a {cost:5}-cost card *causes* you to play a Taskmaster (e.g. you play {card:Haggler} and buy a {cost:5} card, and then gain a Taskmaster with Haggler's ability and play the Taskmaster with {card:Innovation}), that will let the Taskmaster repeat itself on your next turn.
This works if you gain a card by buying it, or if you gain a card in another way (such as {card:Advance} or {card:Charm}).
If you gain a {card:Black Market}, you can play it with {card:Innovation} before taking the {debt:} from its pile.
If you gain a card during another player's Buy phase (e.g. with {card:Messenger}), you won't take the {debt:} on its pile.
It is okay if the pile has a token that does not belong to you or anyone, such as a {vp:} token on {card:Temple} (from Empires).

The pile gets {vp:} even if it is empty; this only matters if there is a way to return a Temple to the pile (like {card:Ambassador} from Dominion: Seaside) or a way to gain one from the trash (like {card:Graverobber} from Dominion: Dark Ages).
If you play this using a Way, or under the influence of {card:Enchantress}, you can still top-deck this when you discard it from play.

If the {card:Clashes} are {card:Hasty} or {card:Patient}, then that may lead you to play Territory. This normally means nothing, but it will still trigger Adventures tokens (e.g. {card:Pathfinding}), count as a card you've played this turn (e.g. for {card:Landing Party}), and counts as a card in play (e.g. for {card:Tools}).

If you happen to put a card on top of your deck in the middle of resolving the Sun's Gift—for instance, by discarding a {card:Tunnel}, gaining a {card:Gold}, and top-decking it due to {card:Progress}—then when you return any remaining cards to your deck they will go on top of the card you just put there.
You cannot play other cards in-between (unless told to by the card, such as with {card:Vassal} or Throne Room itself).

Playing Action cards with Throne Room is just like playing Action cards normally, except it does not use up Action plays for the turn. For example if you start a turn by playing Throne Room on {card:Village}, you would draw a card, get +2 Actions, draw another card, and get +2 Actions again, leaving you with 4 Actions.

If you use Throne Room to play a card that removes itself from the play area, such as {card:Horse} from the Menagerie expansion, Throne Room will still play the card a second time. It will not return to the play area, due to the stop-moving rule; but the card's abilities still take effect as usual. This is a general rule that applies to all "Throne Room variants" that play the same card multiple times on a turn.

However, if the card is worded in such a way that some of its abilities are *contingent* on the card leaving the play area, such as {card:Mining Village} or {card:Madman}, those abilities do not get activated a second time; the card has already moved to wherever it's going, so it can't go there again the second time to reactivate the effect.

If you use Throne Room to play a Duration card, the Throne Room also stays in play until you discard the Duration card. This enables you to track the fact that the Duration card was played multiple times. Even if only one play of the Duration card is keeping it in play, such as using Throne Room on {card:Gear} and only setting aside cards one of the times, Throne Room stays in play with it. If the Duration card leaves play without being discarded (e.g. because you played it with {card:Way of the Horse} on one of its plays), Throne Room is discarded the turn the Duration card leaves play, even if the Duration card has not finished doing things.
This applies both to cards gained due to being bought, and to cards gained other ways, such as with {card:War Chest}.

When you have multiple Duration cards doing things at the start of your turn, you can put them in an order to your advantage; for example if you have four Tide Pools and a {card:Wharf}, you could discard all of your cards to the Tide Pools, then draw the Wharf cards.
If a Tireless card never gets discarded from play (e.g. it's {card:Quartermaster}, {card:Crew}, or a one-shot), then Tireless will have no effect.
If something else moves a Tireless card when it's discarded from play (e.g. {card:Scheme}), you won't set it aside.
If a Tireless card discards itself from play at a weird time (e.g. {card:Highwayman}), you'll still set it aside and put it onto your deck at the end of the turn.

If you have an ability that gives you +Cards at the end of your turn (from e.g. {card:Way of the Squirrel} or {card:Farrier}), you can top-deck your Tireless card before or after taking the +Cards. If you top-deck first, you will draw the Tireless card immediately and it will be in your hand during your opponent's turn.
Note that some things draw extra cards when you draw your Clean-up hand (e.g. {card:Flag} or {card:Expedition}), which will happen before you topdeck Tireless cards.

This works even when it is not your turn, such as when you trash a card to {card:Swindler} (from Dominion: Intrigue), and works when told to trash a card that is not yours, such as with {card:Salt the Earth}.
Cards in play from previous turns are still cards in play; cards you played this turn but which are no longer in play (such as a {card:Pixie} you trashed) are not in play.
So if you play a Tormentor with {card:Overlord}, there are other cards in play (the {card:Overlord} itself), so it gives out a Hex.

If you some how play a Tormentor in such a way that there are no cards in play at all—e.g., you play a Tormentor as {card:Way of the Horse}, and then replay it normally (with {card:Citadel})—there are no *other* cards in play, so you gain an {card:Imp}.

Tracker's top-decking effect kicks in before its Boon-granting effect does, so if the Boon causes you to gain a card, for example a {card:Silver} from {card:The Mountain's Gift}, you can put that card onto your deck.
In games using Tracker, replace one of your starting {card:Copper|Coppers} with a {card:Pouch}.

This card has setup; at the start of games using it, you put a Coin token on each Victory card pile being used (including Kingdom card piles such as {card:Gardens}, and {card:Colony|Colonies} if used).
If you are using the promotional card {card:Black Market}, and Trade Route is in the Black Market deck, you do the setup for Trade Route.
Certain Victory cards come from split piles that are not themselves Victory card piles, such as {card:Dame Josephine} and {card:Territory}; gaining them does not add a token to the Trade Route mat.

The Trade Route token on a pile will *not* move if the top card of a pile is removed without gaining it, such as when you trash it with {card:Salt the Earth}, or exile it with {card:Way of the Worm} or {card:Enclave}.
You get {coin:+} after trashing a card. So if you trash a {card:Hunting Grounds} and gain the first {card:Duchy}, that will increase the {coin:+} you get from this.
If costs are different, such as due to playing {card:Highway}, then Trader will give you a different number of Silvers, based on the current costs.

You still "gained" the card you gained (and not the Silver), for effects that care about gaining a card; for example you could gain {card:Border Village}, use Trader to exchange it for a Silver, then gain a {card:Duchy} using Border Village's ability, and use Trader to exchange that for a Silver too.
If you gain a {card:Mill} with {card:Ironworks} and then exchange it for a Silver, you get +1 Action and +1 Card.
If you gain a Trader to your hand (with e.g. {card:Falconer}), you can exchange the Trader for a Silver.
You can use Trader to exchange a Silver for a Silver. Since exchanging is not gaining, this means the exchanged Silver can avoid getting exiled by a {card:Gatekeeper}.
If you cannot trash Tragic Hero (for example if you play it twice with {card:Throne Room} and trashed it the first time), you still gain the Treasure.

If you trash Trail, playing it means you get the Trail back; it will go into play, and be discarded into your discard pile in that turn's Clean-up. This still counts as trashing it; if you {card:Remodel} a Trail you can play it and then gain a {card:Gold} from Remodel, and so on.
If you gain or trash a Trail during Clean-up (with e.g. {card:Improve}), you can't use its Reaction.

When you are instructed to discard down to a specific handsize (due to a card like {card:Militia} or {card:Marquis}), you first discard all the cards you need to. Then you may play any Trails you discarded; this will increase your handsize again, but you don't have to discard again afterwards.
For example if you trash an Action-Victory card (such as {card:Nobles}, from Dominion: Intrigue), you gain both a {card:Duchy} and a {card:Gold}.
If you Transmute an {card:Estate} under the influence of {card:Inheritance}, you will gain a Gold (for trashing a Victory card) and a Duchy (for trashing an Action card).
For example if the player to your right played {card:Amulet}, gaining a {card:Silver}, then bought a {card:Duchy}, you would gain two Silvers.
Cards "the player to your right gained" include non-Supply cards, like {card:Spoils} or Rewards, as well as cards gained from the Trash, such as through {card:Lurker}.
Cards that are exchanged for, like Travellers or {card:Madman}, are not gained and do not count for this.
Using {card:Throne Room} on Treasure Map is not trashing two Treasure Maps.
If you play a Command variant such as {card:Band of Misfits}, which then plays a Treasure Map, you can't trash the Treasure Map from the Supply, so you will fail to gain 4 Golds.
If you {card:Possession|Possess} someone and make them trash 2 Treasure Maps, both of them are set aside, and you gain 4 Golds to your discard pile.

Both Treasure Maps have to be trashed at once. This means that if you draw the second Treasure Map as a result of trashing the first one (e.g. by trashing a {card:Cultist} to {card:Sewers}), you can't trash the second Treasure Map for 4 Golds.
The {card:Key} does not help you the turn you take it; it gives {coin:+1} at the start of your turn, which has already happened.
When you use a Treasurer to gain a Treasure from the trash, that can trigger abilities like the ones on {card:Ducat} and {card:Spices}.
If you play this with {card:Elder}, you can trash a Treasure and immediately regain it.
If you play Treasurer at the start of your turn (with e.g. {card:Piazza}) and take the {card:Key}, you immediately get {coin:+1} from it.
This only cares about Victory cards gained in the Buy phase, not ones gained in the Action phase (such as via {card:Smugglers}).
So if the player to your left reveals {card:Copper} and {card:Farm}, you get {coin:+4} and +2 cards; if they reveals 2 {card:Silver|Silvers}, you just get {coin:+2}.
After gaining an Estate from this, if you gain a {card:Curse} from another player's {card:Black Cat}, that counts as a card you've gained this turn.
For example, if you had 7 copies of {card:Villa} and 4 copies of {card:Wild Hunt}, you would score {vp:12}.

The tie can be for either first or second place: if you had 7 copies each of Villa and {card:Village}, you would score {vp:21}. If you had 7 copies of Villa, then 4 copies each of Village and Wild Hunt, you would score {vp:12}.
Putting your deck into your discard pile doesn't count as discarding, so it will not activate {card:Tunnel}, {card:Faithful Hound}, or {card:Village Green}.

When you discard multiple cards at once (e.g. to a {card:Minion}), they are all discarded at once. This means if you discard a hand with Tunnel and {card:Watchtower}, you can reveal the Tunnel, but you can't use your Watchtower anymore.
If you do, you gain a {card:Mercenary}.
If you play the same Urchin twice in one turn, such as via {card:Procession}, that does not let you trash it for a Mercenary.

If you play an Urchin, and then you play a Command variant such as {card:Band of Misfits} that plays an Attack from the Supply (such as another Urchin), you may still trash your Urchin for a Mercenary.

It doesn't matter if the effects of the other Attack card, when they are resolved, will actually end up having any effect on your opponents. For instance, if you play a {card:Black Cat} on your own turn, you can still trash an Urchin from play.

Because you trash the Urchin before resolving the Attack, that means if you trash an Urchin by playing a {card:Tormentor}, you'll gain an {card:Imp}. And if you trash an Urchin by playing a {card:Rogue}, you can gain the Urchin from the trash.

You can order Urchin's ability with other "when you play this, first" abilities (e.g. {card:Pathfinding} and {card:Kiln}). These still take place before the other players get to React to the Attack you played (with e.g. {card:Beggar} or {card:Diplomat}).
If you discard a {card:Faithful Hound} with Vassal, you can use Faithful Hound's Reaction ability to set it aside, or use Vassal's ability to play it, but not both.

If you discard a Reaction card that can play itself when discarded, like {card:Weaver}, you can only play it once; it doesn't matter whether you use Vassal's ability or the Reaction card's own ability to do so.
If you gain this during your Action phase, such as with {card:Engineer}, you will put the Villa into your hand and get +1 Action (letting you, for example, play the Villa).

If you gain this during your Buy phase (such as by buying it), you will put the Villa into your hand, get +1 Action, and return to your Action phase. This will let you play more Action cards (such as the Villa). When you are done with that, you will start a new Buy phase, from the beginning — you can play more Treasures (and {card:Arena} will trigger again).
Gaining a Villa during your Buy phase counts as ending it (for cards like {card:Wine Merchant} and {card:Pageant}). If you take multiple Buy phases, those cards will trigger multiple times.

Villa only returns you to your Action phase if gained in your Buy phase. If you gain it at Night (with e.g. {card:Devil's Workshop}) or Clean-up (with e.g. {card:Improve}), it goes to your hand, but you can't play it.

Unlike {card:Ghost Town}, Villa visits the place it is gained to before it moves itself to your hand. This means that when you gain it onto your deck (with e.g. {card:Artificer}), Villa will visit the top of your deck before going into your hand.

Normally, when you gain a Villa while under a {card:Gatekeeper} attack, you can choose to put Villa into your hand first, and Gatekeeper will fail to exile Villa. But if you gain it to your hand (with e.g. {card:Transmogrify}), Gatekeeper will be able to exile it.
If Villa can't put itself into your hand (e.g. because you set it aside with {card:Cargo Ship}), you'll still get +1 Action, and you still return to your Action phase.
Because {card:Replace} and {card:Summon} try to move Villa *after* it is gained and then put into your hand, they will fail to move it.

If you play a Village Green multiple times, such as with {card:Mastermind}, you choose each time whether to take +1 Card and +2 Actions immediately or next turn, and the Village Green only stays in play until next turn if at least one of the plays was for next turn (in which case the Mastermind also stays in play).

You can only discard Village Green if something causes you to or lets you, and discarding it only lets you play it once (each time you discard it). This works whether it is your turn or another player's, and whether you discard it from your hand, or deck (such as with {card:Cardinal}), or from being set aside, or from Exile. This ability does not function if Village Green is put into your discard pile without being discarded, such as when bought, or due to {card:Scavenger} (from Dark Ages).
